title: Robot-assisted partial nephrectomy with venous tumor thrombectomy for classic renal angiomyolipoma: standardized technique and short-term outcomes.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To achieve the dual goals of effective tumor control and maximal renal function preservation, we have proposed a standardized robot-assisted nephron-sparing surgery combined with venous thrombectomy for classic renal angiomyolipoma (AML) with venous tumor thrombus (VTT). This study aimed to evaluate the technical feasibility and clinical rationality of this innovative surgical technique.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 patients who underwent robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) with venous tumor thrombectomy and 16 patients who underwent robot-assisted radical nephrectomy with venous tumor thrombectomy. The radical-nephrectomy cohort served as a historical clinical comparator. The modified thrombectomy strategy followed the proposed "NSS" technical principles. Functional and oncological outcomes were analyzed.

RESULTS: All procedures were completed without open conversion or intraoperative tumor-thrombus dislodgement, and no RAPN case required conversion to radical nephrectomy. The RAPN group had shorter operative time (160.0 vs. 232.5 min, p=0.021), shorter left renal vein clamping (3.0 vs. 16.5 min, p<0.001) and IVC clamping time (3.0 vs. 16.0 min, p<0.001), and better renal function preservation (p<0.001). Renal function was better preserved in RAPN group, primarily reflecting retention of the affected kidney. During the available follow-up (median 9 months in the RAPN group and 55 months in the Control group), no recurrence was detected; however, follow-up was insufficient for comparative or long-term oncological conclusions.

CONCLUSIONS: RAPN with venous tumor thrombectomy appears technically feasible in patients with classic renal AML with VTT. This surgical approach could better preserve renal function, but the long-term outcomes require confirmation in larger series with longer follow-up.

This study aimed to evaluate the technical feasibility and clinical rationality of this innovative surgical technique. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 patients who underwent robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) with venous tumor thrombectomy and 16 patients who underwent robot-assisted radical nephrectomy with venous tumor thrombectomy.

title: Pharmacological strategies for hemodialysis arteriovenous fistula and graft patency: an access-stratified systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pharmacological therapies target different stages of hemodialysis access failure. We compared treatments separately in arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs), accounting for differences in outcomes and follow-up.

METHODS: This PROSPERO-registered review (CRD420261411441) followed PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-NMA guidance. PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL/Cochrane records, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through May 31, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed RoB 2. Separate random-effects frequentist network meta-analyses were supplemented by time-restricted analyses and exploratory follow-up meta-regression.

RESULTS: Among 1,557 records, 31 reports were included; 23 trial datasets contributed to the primary analyses (15 AVF and 8 AVG). In AVFs, ticlopidine (OR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.18-0.76) and clopidogrel (0.49; 0.24-0.97) may reduce predominantly early access failure (low certainty); estimates remained favorable at follow-up of 8 weeks or less. Larger single-trial effects for heparin plus anisodamine and clopidogrel plus a prostacyclin analog were very uncertain. Fish oil showed no clear AVF benefit. In AVGs, apixaban may reduce thrombosis (0.12; 0.03-0.41; low certainty), but its interval widened to 0.007-1.94 in the approximately 12-month subset. The aspirin estimate (3.35; 1.21-9.27) was very uncertain and imprecise under timing restrictions.

CONCLUSIONS: Ticlopidine and clopidogrel may reduce early AVF failure without established improvement in functional maturation. AVG apixaban findings require confirmation, and the effect of aspirin remains very uncertain. Interpretation depends on the clinical outcome, follow-up, and bleeding risk.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Pharmacological therapies target different stages of hemodialysis access failure. We compared treatments separately in arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs), accounting for differences in outcomes and follow-up. METHODS: This PROSPERO-registered review (CRD420261411441) followed PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-NMA guidance.

title: Impact of race, sex, and insurance status on outcomes following endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Racial, sex, and socioeconomic differences in stroke outcomes are well documented, but their associations with outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remain uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with acute ischemic stroke who underwent EVT at a comprehensive stroke center during 2016-2022. The analytic dataset contained 527 patients. Endpoint-specific available observations were used without imputation. Outcomes included expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (eTICI) grade, admission and discharge National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), discharge and 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS), treatment-time metrics, and discharge disposition. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were fitted for seven clinical and procedural endpoints.

RESULTS: Final eTICI grade was available for 493 patients. Successful reperfusion (eTICI ≥2b) occurred in 449 (91.1%), and near-complete reperfusion (eTICI ≥2c) in 309 (62.7%). No demographic or payer variable was significantly associated with either reperfusion endpoint. Poor functional outcome occurred in 344 of 448 patients (76.8%) at discharge and 247 of 376 (65.7%) at 90 days. Black race and Medicare insurance were associated with poor discharge outcome. Female sex, Black race, and Medicare insurance were associated with poor 90-day outcome. Medicare and commercial insurance were associated with non-home discharge. Among 516 patients with available door-to-puncture time, the median was 69 min (interquartile range, 54-91), without statistically significant differences by sex, race, ethnicity, or payer.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing EVT at a single comprehensive stroke center, reperfusion rates were high and were not significantly associated with observed demographic or payer variables. Differences in functional outcomes and discharge destination were observed, but residual confounding, endpoint-specific missingness, and the single-center design limit causal interpretation.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Racial, sex, and socioeconomic differences in stroke outcomes are well documented, but their associations with outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remain uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with acute ischemic stroke who underwent EVT at a comprehensive stroke center during 2016-2022. The analytic dataset contained 527 patients.

title: Effectiveness and Safety of Prophylactic Inferior Vena Cava Filters in High-Risk Hip Fracture Patients: Clinical implications of an early retrieval strategy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of prophylactic inferior vena cava (IVC) filter in patients with hip fracture who were at high risk for pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE).

METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: Single-center Level I Trauma Center.

PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Patients older than 50 years who sustained a low-energy hip fracture (AO/OTA 31A, B, and 32A) and underwent prophylactic IVC filter insertion before hip fracture surgery between 2005 and 2025 were included. Prophylactic IVC filter placement was selectively performed in patients with either objectively confirmed deep vein thrombosis on preoperative screening or absolute contraindications to mechanical and pharmacological venous thromboembolism prophylaxis. Those who had multiple trauma at the time of injury, a clinical follow-up duration ≤6 months after surgery, or undergone IVC filter placement following a confirmed diagnosis of PTE based on pulmonary computed tomography or lung perfusion scanning were excluded.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: The primary outcome was the rate of newly developed symptomatic PTE. Secondary outcomes included IVC filter-related complications, retrieval rates, and 30-day mortality.

RESULTS: One hundred fifty-six patients were included in the prophylactic IVC filter group (39 men 25.0%], 117 women [75.0%]; mean age, 75.8 ± 11.1 years; femoral neck [AO/OTA 31B], n = 71 [45.5%]; intertrochanteric [31A], n = 75 [48.1%]; subtrochanteric [AO/OTA 32A], n = 10 [6.4%];mean indwelling time, 9.1 days; retrieval rate, 88.5%). Among these patients, no cases of newly developed symptomatic PTE were observed (0%), whereas the incidence in the overall hip fracture cohort (n=4,568) was 0.44%. Filter-related complications occurred in 3.9% of patients (minor tilting, 2.6%; vessel adhesion, 1.3%), with no major mechanical failures such as migration or perforation. Although no thrombi were detected at insertion, 4.5% of the patients had trapped thrombi at the time of removal. The 30-day all-cause mortality rate was 1.3% (2/156) in the prophylactic IVC filter group, compared with 1.5% (67/4,568) in the overall hip fracture cohort. (p=0.845). Neither death in the prophylactic IVC filter group was attributed to PTE or an IVC filter-related complication.

CONCLUSIONS: In this study's selected extreme pulmonary thromboembolism risk cohort, including patients with CT-confirmed preoperative DVT, those clinically expected to undergo prolonged perioperative immobilization, or those with contraindications to prophylactic anticoagulation, such as GI bleeding, prophylactic inferior vena cava filter served as an effective and safe temporary bridge therapy rather than a routine prophylactic strategy.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic Level III.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of prophylactic inferior vena cava (IVC) filter in patients with hip fracture who were at high risk for pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE). METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Single-center Level I Trauma Center.

title: Comparative real-world outcomes of LifeStream and Viabahn VBX balloon-expandable covered stents for iliac artery occlusive disease.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Balloon-expandable covered stents (CSs) are increasingly used for complex iliac artery occlusive disease, but direct comparative data among CS platforms remain limited. This study compared 1-year restenosis and clinical outcomes between the LifeStream and Viabahn VBX CSs in patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT).

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 226 patients who underwent EVT for symptomatic iliac artery occlusive disease using either the LifeStream CS (n = 95) or Viabahn VBX CS (n = 131). Outcomes included restenosis, clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR), re-occlusion, conversion to bypass surgery, and perioperative complications (POCs). Between-group comparisons were performed using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) based on propensity scores.

RESULTS: One-year follow-up data were available for 163 of 226 patients (72.1%), and 10 restenosis events occurred during follow-up. After IPTW adjustment, the balance of measured covariates was substantially improved. The estimated 1-year freedom from restenosis was 95.8% (95% confidence interval [CI], 93.1-98.6%) in the LifeStream group and 95.8% (95% CI, 93.1-98.6%) in the Viabahn VBX group, with no statistically significant between-group difference (p = 0.99). No significant differences were detected in freedom from CD-TLR (99.2% [95% CI, 98.0-100.0%] vs. 96.7% [95% CI, 94.3-99.2%]; p = 0.13), re-occlusion (100.0% [95% CI, 100.0-100.0%] vs. 98.1% [95% CI, 96.3-99.9%]; p = 0.091), conversion to bypass surgery (100.0% [95% CI, 100.0-100.0%] vs. 98.2% [95% CI, 96.4-100.0%]; p = 0.083), or POCs.

CONCLUSION: In this IPTW-adjusted multicenter retrospective study, no statistically significant differences in 1-year restenosis or other clinical outcomes were detected between the LifeStream and Viabahn VBX balloon-expandable CSs. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating because of the small number of events, incomplete follow-up, and potential residual confounding.

This study compared 1-year restenosis and clinical outcomes between the LifeStream and Viabahn VBX CSs in patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT). METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 226 patients who underwent EVT for symptomatic iliac artery occlusive disease using either the LifeStream CS (n = 95) or Viabahn VBX CS (n = 131).

title: Impact of Inherited Thrombophilia on Cancer-associated Thrombosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer-associated thrombosis (CT) is a cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with malignancy. The contribution of inherited thrombophilia remains incompletely defined.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between inherited thrombophilia and other genetic determinants and CT risk in adults with malignancy.

METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies comparing genetic determinants in patients with cancer with and without venous thromboembolism (VTE). Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using Mantel-Haenszel models. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE), respectively.

RESULTS: Twenty-one studies including 4,479 patients (1,115 with VTE) were included. Factor V Leiden (FVL) was associated with increased odds of CT (OR 2.48, 95% CI: 1.75-3.51; I 2 = 32%), with consistent findings after exclusion of device- or catheter-related thrombosis. Heterozygous FVL was associated with CT (OR 1.86, 95% CI: 1.27-2.73), whereas the homozygous estimate was imprecise (OR 3.42, 95% CI: 0.75-15.59). Prothrombin G20210A was associated with CT (OR 2.67, 95% CI: 1.56-4.58; I 2 = 0%). Exploratory analyses yielded estimates for methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR; OR 1.40, 95% CI: 1.02-1.93) and blood group O (OR 0.40, 95% CI 0.23-0.70); the latter was based on only two studies. Evidence for rarer determinants was sparse. Certainty was moderate for FVL and low or very low for other determinants.

CONCLUSION: FVL and prothrombin G20210A are associated with increased odds of CT. Current evidence does not support universal genetic screening but warrants prospective evaluation of the incremental predictive value of genetic markers beyond established CT risk models.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Cancer-associated thrombosis (CT) is a cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with malignancy. The contribution of inherited thrombophilia remains incompletely defined. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between inherited thrombophilia and other genetic determinants and CT risk in adults with malignancy.

title: Vascular risk prediction in migraine: A multimodality risk score based on artificial intelligence-electrocardiogram output, echocardiogram, and detailed migraine characteristics.
abstract: AimPatients with migraine, especially those with aura, have a higher risk of stroke and other vascular events. However, the underlying mechanisms are complex, multifactorial, and may require integration of multimodal data for comprehensive characterization. We have conducted prior analyses on how artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled electrocardiogram (ECG), specifically the atrial fibrillation prediction model and age estimation model output, echocardiogram parameters, and detailed migraine characteristics separately predict vascular events. Herein, we aim to investigate the relative importance and combined effects of all three modalities for vascular risk prediction.MethodsIn this retrospective cohort study, we developed a multimodality prediction risk score to evaluate the vascular risks in patients with migraine based on the coefficients of variables extracted from our prior studies, including comprehensive AI-ECG atrial fibrillation prediction model output and computed delta age (ECG estimated age minus chronological age), echocardiogram parameters, and migraine characteristics. We then included patients with at least one 12-lead ECG, transthoracic echocardiogram, and a visit with a headache specialist at any Mayo Clinic site within three years to evaluate the risk score. The outcome is a composite endpoint of acute ischemic stroke, acute myocardial infarction, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality. We selected 20 risk parameters, including demographics, comorbidities, AI-ECG outputs, echocardiogram features, and migraine characteristics found to be predictive of vascular events. Each variable was assigned a different risk score according to the hazard ratio (HR) and beta coefficient from prior Cox regression analysis for each modality. We used Contal and Q'Quigley's method to find the optimal cut-off, and an additional multivariate Cox regression was conducted to assess the relative risk of each parameter category in the final cohort. We investigated the added value of each modality by net reclassification improvement rate.ResultsA total of 29,928 patients, 12,778 patients, and 6819 patients were included to investigate how AI-ECG outputs, echocardiogram parameters, and migraine characteristics, respectively, predicted adverse vascular outcomes, and the results were used to develop a multimodal risk score. A total of 297 patients with migraine included in previous analyses, of whom 247 (83.2%) were female and 109 (36.7%) had aura, were used for proof-of-concept evaluation of the developed risk score. The mean (standard deviation, SD) age was 39.0 (13.3) and follow-up period was 68.9 (60.9) months. Thirty-five patients (11.8%) developed the composite endpoint. Those with a risk score ≥15 had a significantly shorter vascular event-free survival (HR [95% Confidence Interval (CI)], 3.83 [1.89-7.76]; p < 0.001) compared to those with a risk score <15 in our cohort of 297 patients. Furthermore, comorbidity (HR, 1.17 [1.06-1.30]; p = 0.003) and migraine characteristics (HR, 1.33 [1.06-1.67]; p = 0.014) were significantly predictive of the composite endpoint, whereas other categories were not. Net reclassification improvement was 17.7% (95% CI, 15.9-19.9%; p < 0.001) for AI-ECG model output, 16.9% (95% CI, 14.1-19.5%; p < 0.001) for echocardiogram, and 22.1% (95% CI, 16.7-26.9%; p < 0.001) for migraine characteristics, suggesting significant contribution from each modality.ConclusionThis pilot evaluation study supports the use of combined AI-ECG output, echocardiogram, and migraine characteristics for vascular risk prediction. Although future external validation and real-world clinical assessment is necessary, our preliminary results suggest significant added value of each modality and indicate the importance of obtaining detailed migraine features for vascular risk stratification.

However, the underlying mechanisms are complex, multifactorial, and may require integration of multimodal data for comprehensive characterization. We have conducted prior analyses on how artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled electrocardiogram (ECG), specifically the atrial fibrillation prediction model and age estimation model output, echocardiogram parameters, and detailed migraine characteristics separately predict vascular events.

title: Development and Internal Validation of an Integrated Clinical, Laboratory, and Ultrasound Model for 30-Day Venous Thromboembolic Deterioration After Acute Lower-Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis.
abstract: BackgroundShort-term prognostic tools for venous thromboembolic (VTE) deterioration after acute lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) are limited. We aimed to develop and internally validate a model integrating clinical, laboratory, and duplex ultrasound characteristics.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort included 785 adults with ultrasound-confirmed acute lower-extremity DVT from January 2018 to December 2025. The primary outcome was clinically detected and objectively confirmed ipsilateral DVT progression or new-onset symptomatic pulmonary embolism (PE) within 30 days. Three nested ridge-penalized logistic models included clinical predictors (Model 1), clinical plus laboratory predictors (Model 2), and clinical, laboratory, and ultrasound predictors (Model 3). Missing data were multiply imputed, and the complete modeling procedure was internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Discrimination, calibration, Brier score, incremental performance, and decision-curve net benefit were assessed.ResultsThe primary outcome occurred in 102 patients (13.0%): 82 had DVT progression and 27 symptomatic PE, with seven having both. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.702, 0.766, and 0.808 (95% CI, 0.769-0.847) for Models 1-3, respectively. For Model 3, the optimism-corrected calibration slope was 0.94 and Brier score 0.087. Optimism-corrected ΔAUCs were 0.064 and 0.042, with corresponding ΔBrier scores of -0.009 and -0.008. Model 3 showed the highest optimism-corrected net benefit across thresholds of approximately 8%-25%. Observed outcome proportions across risk tertiles were 3.1%, 9.6%, and 26.3%.ConclusionsModel 3 provided internally validated prediction of clinically detected VTE deterioration under local treatment and imaging practices. External validation and prospective clinical-impact assessment are required before routine use.

We aimed to develop and internally validate a model integrating clinical, laboratory, and duplex ultrasound characteristics.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort included 785 adults with ultrasound-confirmed acute lower-extremity DVT from January 2018 to December 2025. The primary outcome was clinically detected and objectively confirmed ipsilateral DVT progression or new-onset symptomatic pulmonary embolism (PE) within 30 days.

title: A Two-Step Risk Stratification Model for Venous Thromboembolism Combining Caprini Score and D-Dimer in Trauma Patients Undergoing Surgery.
abstract: ObjectiveTo determine whether adding D-dimer to Caprini score-based risk assessment can further refine venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk stratification in trauma patients, particularly among those already classified as high-risk.MethodsA retrospective cohort of 206 trauma surgical patients who underwent surgical intervention was analyzed. Caprini scores and baseline plasma D-dimer levels were assessed against VTE occurrence using ROC curves. The two-step strategy consisted of initial Caprini-based stratification, followed by secondary D-dimer re-stratification using a study-derived exploratory threshold derived from the Youden index within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (Caprini score ≥9) in the same cohort. This threshold was not externally validated. All patients received mechanical VTE prophylaxis, while patients with Caprini scores ≥9 received prophylactic-dose low-molecular-weight heparin. Bilateral lower-extremity Doppler ultrasound was performed within 24 hours of admission, with subsequent surveillance according to predefined risk criteria.ResultsOverall composite VTE incidence was 31.1%. The Caprini score showed an AUC of 0.640 for VTE discrimination. D-dimer showed the highest discrimination in the full cohort (AUC = 0.669), which decreased to 0.614 within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (≥9 points, n = 118). Applying a study-derived exploratory D-dimer threshold of ≥5.5 mg/L identified a subgroup with a higher observed VTE incidence (44.8% vs. 16.1%; RR = 2.78, 95% CI: 1.21-6.37, P = 0.005). However, after adjustment for age, sex, and ISS, the association was attenuated and did not remain statistically significant (adjusted OR = 2.418, 95% CI: 0.660-8.864, P = 0.183).ConclusionsRelying solely on clinical risk scoring provides limited VTE discrimination in trauma patients. A sequential two-step strategy identified a subgroup with a higher observed VTE incidence within the Caprini high-risk category, although an independent association between the D-dimer threshold and VTE was not demonstrated after adjustment. This approach warrants prospective validation in larger cohorts.

Caprini scores and baseline plasma D-dimer levels were assessed against VTE occurrence using ROC curves. The two-step strategy consisted of initial Caprini-based stratification, followed by secondary D-dimer re-stratification using a study-derived exploratory threshold derived from the Youden index within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (Caprini score ≥9) in the same cohort.

title: Heat-Based Therapies in Hypertension Management: A Systematic Review of Physiological Mechanisms.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for several cardiovascular diseases, leading to the need for investigations of user-friendly and less costly nonpharmacological interventions, including passive heat therapies. This study synthesized information on heat-based therapies used in prehypertension and hypertension management, as well as their clinical efficacy, physiological mechanisms, and translational potential.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed 13 eligible human studies published between 2000 and 2025 per the PRISMA 2020 checklist, assessed randomized studies with RoB 2 and nonrandomized studies with ROBINS-I, and used SWiM-guided narrative synthesis because interventions, populations, comparators, and outcomes were heterogeneous. Certainty was assessed using GRADE. The review protocol was not preregistered.

RESULTS: Acute blood-pressure reductions and changes in vascular or autonomic markers were reported in some populations, but sustained comparative effects in hypertension remain uncertain. In hypertensive participants, both hot and thermoneutral immersion were associated with reductions in 24-h blood pressure (BP), limiting heat-specific attribution. A single pooled effect estimate and corresponding 95% confidence interval were not calculated. The benefits were linked to lower sympathetic activity, more nitric oxide availability, lower endothelin-1 levels, and less oxidative stress. Outcome-specific GRADE certainty was very low for SBP and DBP and the assessed mechanistic domains.

CONCLUSION: Passive heat exposure can produce short-term reductions in BP and changes in vascular function, but sustained antihypertensive efficacy, particularly when evaluated with 24-h ambulatory BP in patients with established hypertension, remains uncertain. Mechanistic findings from heart-failure and peripheral artery disease (PAD) cohorts are indirect evidence for uncomplicated hypertension. Passive heat should not replace established antihypertensive treatment. Safety evidence is limited to selected, often supervised populations, and larger trials with ambulatory BP and systematic adverse-event assessment are needed.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed 13 eligible human studies published between 2000 and 2025 per the PRISMA 2020 checklist, assessed randomized studies with RoB 2 and nonrandomized studies with ROBINS-I, and used SWiM-guided narrative synthesis because interventions, populations, comparators, and outcomes were heterogeneous.

title: Anterior mitral leaflet modification to prevent left ventricular outflow tract obstruction during transcatheter mitral valve replacement: the PROTECT-LVOT registry.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction remains the major limitation of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Anterior mitral leaflet (AML) modification has emerged as a key preventive strategy, yet real-world data remain limited and residual risk is still unknown.

AIMS: We sought to evaluate the outcomes of TMVR with concomitant AML modification across valve-in-mitral annular calcification (ViMAC), valve-in-ring (ViR), and valve-in-valve (ViV) substrates.

METHODS: We established a multicentre retrospective registry of consecutive patients undergoing TMVR with AML modification between 2017 and 2025. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, stroke/transient ischaemic attack, and major bleeding.

RESULTS: A total of 55 patients were included (67% females). The median age was 78 years (interquartile range [IQR] 73-81); the median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality was 6.7% (IQR 4.8-9.5). AML modification was performed in 65.5% of cases with the Laceration of the Anterior Mitral leaflet to Prevent Outflow ObstructioN technique and in 34.5% with the Balloon-Assisted Translocation of the Mitral Anterior Leaflet technique. AML modification was successful in 96.4% of cases. Despite successful AML modification, haemodynamically significant LVOT obstruction occurred in 12.7% of cases. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint occurred in 20.0% of patients, driven by cardiovascular death in 14.5% of patients. Overall in-hospital mortality was 16.4%. The ViMAC substrate was associated with the numerically highest LVOT obstruction rate (ViMAC 20.7%, ViR 0.0%, ViV 8.3%, odds ratio [OR] 4.72, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.89-47.86; p=0.070). The aortomitral angle showed a borderline association with LVOT obstruction (OR 1.22 per degree, 95% CI: 0.99-1.48; p=0.059).

CONCLUSIONS: AML modification enables TMVR in high-risk anatomies with high feasibility but does not eliminate LVOT obstruction. ViMAC represents the most challenging substrate.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction remains the major limitation of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Anterior mitral leaflet (AML) modification has emerged as a key preventive strategy, yet real-world data remain limited and residual risk is still unknown. AIMS: We sought to evaluate the outcomes of TMVR with concomitant AML modification across valve-in-mitral annular calcification (ViMAC), valve-in-ring (ViR), and valve-in-valve (ViV) substrates.

title: Repurposing drugs for aortic aneurysm: unlocking new therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a life-threatening vascular disease for which no pharmacological therapy has been proven to effectively limit disease progression. Drug repurposing (DR), which leverages existing drugs with established safety profiles, offers a promising and cost-effective strategy to accelerate therapeutic development for AA. In this review, we summarize recent advances in DR research for AA, highlighting the emerging framework that integrates computational prediction with experimental and clinical validation. We discuss key repurposed drug candidates, evaluate the current state of translational evidence, and examine the challenges that have hindered clinical success despite encouraging preclinical findings. Finally, we outline opportunities to enhance target identification, patient stratification, and clinical trial design. By bridging mechanistic discovery and translational application, DR may provide a practical pathway toward effective medical therapies for aneurysmal disease.

Drug repurposing (DR), which leverages existing drugs with established safety profiles, offers a promising and cost-effective strategy to accelerate therapeutic development for AA. In this review, we summarize recent advances in DR research for AA, highlighting the emerging framework that integrates computational prediction with experimental and clinical validation.

title: Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative Contemporary Benchmarks: Thoracic Endovascular Aortic Repair.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe contemporary outcomes as well as temporal trends of in-hospital mortality and complication rates for patients undergoing thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) across indications and levels of urgency, establishing a benchmark for future analytic efforts.

METHODS: The VQI TEVAR and complex EVAR registry was queried for procedures performed between January 2014-December 2024. Primary outcomes included in-hospital mortality and major complications. Analyses were stratified by indication to include descending thoracic aortic aneurysms (DTAA), dissections, and trauma. Aneurysms involving the aortic arch (i.e. landing zone < 2) or extending to the visceral segment and distally (i.e. landing zone >5) were excluded. Linear regression and the Cochran Armitage test for trend were used to analyze yearly mortality and complication rates over time. Mortality and complication end-points were further analyzed using logistic regression with and without risk-adjustment.

RESULTS: Over the ten-year study period, 4,632 TEVARs were performed for DTAA, 6,701 for dissection, and 2,321 for trauma. For patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA, in-hospital mortality declined significantly for both elective (2014, 3.9% versus 2024, 1.0%, -0.26 percentage points per year, p=0.01) and nonelective cases (2014, 16.7% versus 2024, 8.7%, -0.63 percentage points per year, p=0.04). There was also a decline in in-hospital mortality among elective dissection patients (2014, 3.7% versus 2024, 0.5%, -0.17 percentage points per year, p=0.03). Elective TEVAR overall is associated with a mortality rate of less than two percent per year. The in-hospital complication trends declined significantly for patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA - elective patients experienced a decline in complication rates by -1.13 percentage points per year (2014, 24.8% versus 2024, 11.5% p<0.001) and non-elective patients experienced a decline in complication rates by -2.0 percentage points per year (2014, 40.5% versus 2024, 25.2%, p<0.001). Dissection patients undergoing elective repair had a decrease of -0.8 percentage points per year (2014, 16.9% versus 2024, 9.2%, p<0.001). Nonelective dissections repairs had a complication rate of 36.4% in 2014 vs 34.1% in 2024, p=0.874). Trauma patients tended toward higher complication rates over time, with a rate of 21.6% in 2014 and 32.2% in 2024, p=0.06) Trauma patients experienced an overall increase in in-hospital mortality of +0.38 percentage points per year (2014, 9.8% versus 2024, 9.4%, p=0.01).

CONCLUSION: Temporal trends within the VQI demonstrate improvements in mortality and complication rates for patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA and elective dissection repair, with contemporary yearly mortality rates of less than two percent. Patients undergoing non-elective dissection repair and those with traumatic indications represent challenging and complex pathologies requiring further research to identify opportunities to improve outcomes.

METHODS: The VQI TEVAR and complex EVAR registry was queried for procedures performed between January 2014-December 2024. Primary outcomes included in-hospital mortality and major complications.

title: Final 5-year results of the Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis Feasibility Trials for Treatment of Aortic Arch Aneurysms.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report final 5-year outcomes from prospective multicenter feasibility studies of the GORE® TAG® Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis (TBE) for aneurysms involving the proximal descending thoracic aorta and aortic arch (zones 0-2).

METHODS: Forty consecutive patients (23 male; mean age, 74±10 years) were enrolled at six sites in prospective, nonrandomized feasibility trials (2014-2016). Patients underwent TEVAR with proximal TBE in zone 0/1 (n=9; NCT02264977) or zone 2 (n=31; NCT02021812). A clinical events committee adjudicated aneurysm-related and all-cause mortality, major adverse events, and cerebrovascular events. Core laboratory analysis assessed endoleaks (types I-IV), aneurysm sac enlargement, device migration, and side branch patency. Five-year cumulative risk rates (2006 days) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

RESULTS: The median follow-up time among survivors was 60.2 months (range, 25.8 to 66.0), with 17 patients completing the required 5-year clinical and imaging follow-up across both studies. Eleven late deaths occurred; KM-estimated cumulative risk of 5-year all-cause mortality was 29% (95% CI: 17%-46%). One zone 2 death was adjudicated as aortic-related (2.5%; 95% CI: 0.4%-16%) due to ascending aortic rupture, with no ruptures occurring within treated aortic segments. Reintervention risk through 5 years was low (KM-estimated cumulative risk, 5.1%; 95% CI: 1.3%-19%), with two events, both in the zone 2 cohort. Five patients experienced stroke events through 5 years, corresponding to a KM cumulative risk of 19.0% ( 95% CI: 7.2%-43%), two in zone 2 and three in zone 0/1. Two patients had target vessel instability (5.0%, 95% CI: 0.6%-16.9%). Two side-branch patency events occurred in zone 2: one complete side-branch occlusion in the LSA associated with transient mild arm claudication and one asymptomatic partial occlusion, primary patency through 5-year follow-up was 94.8% (37/39 evaluable patients). Core laboratory identified endoleaks in 12 patients (30.8%; 95% CI: 15%-45%). Three patients (7.7%) had a type I or III endoleak by 5 years, all in the zone 2 arm; these included type IA in one patient (2.6%) and type III in two patients (5.1%). Additionally indeterminate (n=8, 20.5%) and type II (n=6, 15.4%) endoleaks were observed. Cumulative risk rate of aneurysm sac enlargement through 5-years was 15.0% for all patients (95% CI: 5.6%-30.3%), with events occurring in three zone 2 patients and one zone 0/1 patient.

CONCLUSIONS: At 5 years, the early feasibility studies demonstrated excellent side branch patency, a low incidence of type IA endoleak, low aortic-related mortality, and no rupture within the treated aortic segments. Larger studies are needed to better define zone-specific cerebrovascular risk and long-term durability.

METHODS: Forty consecutive patients (23 male; mean age, 74±10 years) were enrolled at six sites in prospective, nonrandomized feasibility trials (2014-2016). title: The Effects of Non-Psoriatic Dermatitis on Total Hip Arthroplasty Outcomes: A Propensity-Matched Analysis with Longitudinal Follow-Up.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: While psoriasis has been associated with increased complications following total hip arthroplasty (THA), the effects of non-psoriatic dermatitis (NPD) on THA outcomes remain unclear. Therefore, this study evaluated the association between NPD and postoperative outcomes following primary THA with additional stratification by dermatitis-related medication use.

METHODS: In a large national database, patients aged ≥ 18 years undergoing primary THA anytime between 2003 and 2020 were identified. Patients who had NPD were compared with a control cohort of patients who did not have NPD. Additional pairwise comparisons evaluated the effect of dermatitis-related medication use. After multiple demographics and comorbidities were propensity-matched using a 1:1 ratio, postoperative medical outcomes and surgical complications were examined with follow-up at 90 days, one year, and two years.

RESULTS: At 90 days, NPD was associated with a higher rate of emergency department admission and a lower rate of periprosthetic dislocation or instability (P ≤ 0.048). There were no other significant associations observed at one or two years. Compared to patients who do not have NPD, patients who have NPD with concurrent medication use had higher rates of inpatient readmission, emergency department admission, deep vein thrombosis, falls, and periprosthetic fracture at 90 days (P ≤ 0.027), and periprosthetic fracture remained elevated at one and two years (P ≤ 0.012). Patients who have NPD without medication use showed no significant differences for all measured outcomes across every timepoint.

CONCLUSION: Although some 90-day outcomes were significant, NPD was not independently associated with one- and two-year complications following THA. Patients receiving medications for NPD treatment may represent a high-risk subgroup with increased healthcare utilization, thromboembolic events, falls, and periprosthetic fracture. Among THA candidates who have NPD, the effects of pharmaceutical management may be considered, especially for thromboembolic risk, fall prevention, and bone health optimization.

title: Impact of COVID-19 surgical delays on chronic venous disease: a multicenter observational study in France.
abstract: IntroductionCOVID-19 lockdowns led to widespread postponement of elective procedures, including endovenous interventions for chronic venous disease (CVD). This study aimed to evaluate the clinical impact of delayed thermal ablation in a real-world French multicenter cohort.MethodsThis prospective, multicenter observational study included 203 adults with documented great or small saphenous vein insufficiency or recurrent varicose veins whose endovenous procedures were postponed during the 2020-2021 lockdowns. Clinical severity was assessed using the Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS) and CEAP classification at the postponement assessment and at the rescheduling assessment. The primary analysis was performed on patients with a VCSS available at both time points. Paired t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used to assess within-patient change over time.ResultsAmong 203 enrolled patients, 86 (42.4%) had a VCSS available at both time points and were included in the primary analysis. The median delay between the postponement and rescheduling assessments was 80 days (IQR 69-101). Mean VCSS remained unchanged (5.4±3.0 vs 5.4±2.8; mean difference 0.0, 95% CI -0.4 to 0.4). CEAP classification was stable in 89.5% of patients, with no significant overall shift (p = 0.246). Adverse events occurred in 3.5% of cases, mainly superficial vein thrombosis. Physicians reported a negative impact of the delay in 60% of assessments, and a physician-perceived potential loss of therapeutic opportunity in 7.5% of the full cohort (n = 199) and 20.9% of the paired cohort at rescheduling (n = 86).ConclusionIn this real-world cohort, delayed endovenous treatment for CVD was not associated with clinically evident short-term deterioration in this sample. However, the high rate of missing paired data, the resulting risk of selection bias, and limited statistical power mean that a clinically relevant effect cannot be excluded. These findings suggest relative clinical stability in mild-to-moderate CVD during short-term delays, but further adequately powered studies are required.

Clinical severity was assessed using the Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS) and CEAP classification at the postponement assessment and at the rescheduling assessment.

title: Association between low-dose glucocorticoid administration during anesthesia induction and neurological improvement in patients with spinal dural arteriovenous fistula: a propensity score-matched cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-dose glucocorticoid treatment before the diagnosis of spinal dural arteriovenous fistula (SDAVF) has been associated with acute neurological worsening, but the association of a single, comparatively low dose administered during anesthesia induction with long-term neurological recovery remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between glucocorticoid administration during anesthesia induction and neurological improvement after definitive treatment.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included patients with angiographically confirmed SDAVF treated between March 2013 and July 2021. Neurological improvement was defined as a decrease of at least 1 point in the modified Aminoff-Logue Scale score from pretreatment to the last follow-up. Patients were matched 1:1 without replacement and exactly by treatment modality using propensity scores based on age, sex, disease duration, and pretreatment neurological function. Between-group differences were evaluated using the paired risk difference, exact McNemar test, and modified Poisson regression. Glucocorticoid type and equivalent dexamethasone dose (EDD) were also evaluated among glucocorticoid-treated patients.

RESULTS: The cohort included 428 patients, of whom 172 received glucocorticoids and 256 did not. Propensity-score matching retained 167 pairs. Neurological improvement occurred in 118 of 167 patients (70.7%) in the glucocorticoid group and 119 of 167 patients (71.3%) in the nonglucocorticoid group. The paired risk difference was - 0.6 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], - 10.4 to 9.2; exact McNemar P = 1.000). Glucocorticoid administration was not associated with neurological improvement in the adjusted modified Poisson model (risk ratio [RR], 0.996; 95% CI, 0.871-1.138; P = 0.947), and sensitivity analyses yielded consistent findings. Among matched glucocorticoid-treated patients, neither glucocorticoid type (dexamethasone vs. methylprednisolone: adjusted RR, 0.979; 95% CI, 0.666-1.441; P = 0.916) nor EDD (per 5-mg increase: adjusted RR, 1.022; 95% CI, 0.931-1.121; P = 0.646) was associated with neurological improvement.

CONCLUSION: A single, comparatively low glucocorticoid dose administered during anesthesia induction was not associated with neurological improvement at the last follow-up after definitive treatment of SDAVF. No clear associations were identified for glucocorticoid type or EDD.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: High-dose glucocorticoid treatment before the diagnosis of spinal dural arteriovenous fistula (SDAVF) has been associated with acute neurological worsening, but the association of a single, comparatively low dose administered during anesthesia induction with long-term neurological recovery remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between glucocorticoid administration during anesthesia induction and neurological improvement after definitive treatment. METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included patients with angiographically confirmed SDAVF treated between March 2013 and July 2021.

title: Endovascular robotic-assisted system for cerebral angiography (ERASE): Rationale, design, and protocol of a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Neurointerventional therapy is a cornerstone in managing head and neck vascular disorders, with cerebral angiography serving as its fundamental diagnostic and therapeutic backbone. However, manual cerebral angiography is associated with several inherent limitations. While existing robotic-assisted systems have shown promise in mitigating some of these issues, they face challenges such as limited compatibility, lengthy setup times, and a lack of high-quality real-world evidence. The ERASE trial is a multicenter, prospective, randomized controlled trial (RCT). A total of 660 eligible patients will be enrolled from seven comprehensive stroke centers in China and randomized 1:1 to either the robotic-assisted group or the control group. Both groups use the Seldinger technique for femoral/radial artery access. Operators undergo standardized training on the robotic system. The trial adopts a prospective randomized open-label blinded endpoint (PROBE) design, with all imaging endpoints adjudicated via blinded review by an independent imaging core laboratory. All patients are followed up at baseline, end of surgery, 24 h postoperatively, and 7 days post-discharge. The primary efficacy outcome is the clinical success rate. The primary safety outcome is the incidence of perioperative/postoperative complications (e.g., vascular perforation, dissection, pseudoaneurysm), serious adverse events, and device malfunctions. Secondary outcomes include technical failure rate, overall procedural time, pre-puncture setup time, mean catheterization time per target vessel, super-selective technique success rate, DSA fluoroscopy time, participant radiation dose, primary operator radiation dose, contrast agent volume and instrument performance evaluation. A key safety endpoint is the rate of new asymptomatic cerebral infarctions detected via postoperative brain MRI-diffusion-weighted imaging. As the RCT focusing on the YDHB-NS01 Ver 2.0 system, the ERASE trial addresses critical unmet needs in neurointerventional practice and will generate high-quality evidence for robotic-assisted cerebral angiography. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07182188. TRIAL REGISTRATION DATE: 2025-09-18.

title: [Effect of sequential multi-dose tranexamic acid administration on perioperative blood loss in cervical posterior single-door laminoplasty and its safety].
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effect of sequential multi-dose intravenous administration of tranexamic acid (TXA) on perioperative blood loss and inflammatory response in patients undergoing cervical posterior single-door laminoplasty (LMP), and to evaluate its safety.

METHODS: A prospective study was conducted in patients diagnosed with multi-level cervical spondylotic myelopathy, who underwent cervical posterior single-door LMP between January 2023 and June 2024. Using a computer-generated randomization table, patients were allocated into three groups. Placebo control group (group A): received 100 mL of normal saline intravenously at 30 minutes before incision (after anesthesia induction); the same dose was repeated every 5 hours for a total of 3 administrations. Single-dose control group (group B): received 1.0 g of TXA (dissolved in 100 mL normal saline) at 30 minutes before incision, followed by 100 mL of normal saline every 5 hours for a total of 2 additional doses. Sequential multi-dose group (group C): received 1.0 g of TXA (dissolved in 100 mL normal saline) at 30 minutes before incision, with an additional 1.0 g of TXA administered intravenously at 5 hours and 10 hours postoperatively, for a total dose of 3.0 g. A total of 120 patients met the selection criteria and were included in the study. After excluding lost-to-follow-up and withdrawn patients, 39 cases in group A, 37 in group B, and 38 in group C were included in the final analysis. There was no significant difference between groups (P>0.05) in age, gender, height, body weight, body mass index, comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes), and preoperative hematocrit (HCT), hemoglobin, D-dimer (D-D), interleukin 6 (IL-6), and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. The primary outcome was total blood loss (TBL). Secondary outcomes included intraoperative blood loss (IBL), postoperative blood loss (PBL), drain removal time (DRT), HCT, D-D, IL-6, CRP, allogeneic blood transfusion rate, and incidence of complications.

RESULTS: Blood loss assessment: TBL, PBL, DRT, postoperative decline in HCT, and the allogeneic blood transfusion rate were all the lowest in group C, followed by group B, and the highest in group A, with significant differences between groups (P<0.05). The IBL was significantly lower in groups B and C than in group A (P<0.05), while there was no significant difference between groups B and C (P>0.05). Changes in inflammatory indicators: the levels of D-D and IL-6 in 3 groups reached peak at 1 day, the level of CRP reached peak at 3 days, and both decreased at 5 days, but still remained higher than preoperative levels, with significant differences (P<0.05). At different time points, the levels of D-D, IL-6, and CRP were significant lower in group C than in groups A and B (P<0.05), and in group B than in group A (P<0.05). Safety evaluation: During the 30-day postoperative follow-up, no deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, incisional infection, incisional hematoma, or TXA-related allergic reaction occurred in 3 groups.

CONCLUSION: Sequential multi-dose TXA administration effectively reduces perioperative blood loss in cervical posterior single-door LMP, suppresses postoperative hyperfibrinolysis and inflammatory response, shortens drainage duration, and does not increase the risk of thromboembolic events. This regimen represents a safe and effective optimization strategy for perioperative blood management in LMP.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effect of sequential multi-dose intravenous administration of tranexamic acid (TXA) on perioperative blood loss and inflammatory response in patients undergoing cervical posterior single-door laminoplasty (LMP), and to evaluate its safety. METHODS: A prospective study was conducted in patients diagnosed with multi-level cervical spondylotic myelopathy, who underwent cervical posterior single-door LMP between January 2023 and June 2024. Using a computer-generated randomization table, patients were allocated into three groups.

title: Effect of Different Single-Session Durations of Intermittent Pneumatic Compression on the Prevention of Deep Vein Thrombosis in Postoperative ICU Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a common and potentially life-threatening complication in postoperative ICU patients. Intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) is widely used for mechanical thromboprophylaxis; however, the optimal single-session duration of IPC remains unclear. This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy of different single-session durations of IPC for preventing DVT in postoperative ICU patients. MATERIAL AND METHODS This prospective randomized controlled trial enrolled 138 patients who were randomized into 3 groups (n = 46 each) receiving IPC 3 times daily, with single-session durations of 40 minutes, 2 hours, or 6 hours. DVT incidence, coagulation parameters (D-dimer [mg/L] and fibrinogen [FIB; g/L]), and adverse events were compared on postoperative days 3 and 5. RESULTS Baseline characteristics were comparable among groups (P>0.05). The 6-hour group had a DVT incidence of 0% on both days, significantly lower than those in the 40-minute (15.21% and 32.61%) and 2-hour (8.70% and 34.78%) groups (P<0.05). No significant intergroup differences in D-dimer levels were observed (P>0.05); FIB levels significantly differed only on day 3 (P<0.05). Adverse events occurred in 6 patients (13.04%) in the 6-hour group, whereas none occurred in the other 2 groups. CONCLUSIONS Although 6-hour single-session IPC provides the most effective DVT prevention, it is associated with a higher risk of skin-related adverse events. Shorter, more frequent IPC (40 minutes or 2 hours per session, 3 times daily) may represent a preferable strategy for postoperative ICU patients due to its balance of efficacy, safety, and clinical feasibility.

Intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) is widely used for mechanical thromboprophylaxis; however, the optimal single-session duration of IPC remains unclear. This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy of different single-session durations of IPC for preventing DVT in postoperative ICU patients.

title: Risk factors associated with the development of a catheter-related thrombosis in patients with critical illness: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
PURPOSE: We sought to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis with the primary objective to identify prognostic factors associated with developing a catheter-related thrombosis in the critical care setting. Our secondary objective was to report the incidence of this entity.

SOURCES: We searched, MEDLINE® and Embase® from inception through 4 May 2024 for all studies in patients with critical illness that reported catheter-related thrombosis, with an updated search performed on 23 October 2025. We included English-language studies that described prognostic factors for developing a catheter-related thrombosis or reported the incidence of this complication in the critical care setting. Two authors performed citation screening and data extraction. We pooled adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) separately for prognostic factors using a random-effects model and inverse variance weighting. Risk of bias for individual studies was evaluated using the Quality in Prognosis Studies tool. We assessed certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations approach.

PRINCIPLE FINDINGS: We included 32 studies involving 11,943 patients. Identified prognostic variables with a moderate- or high-certainty association for developing a catheter-related thrombosis include increasing age (aOR per 10-yr increase, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06 to 1.27; three studies; 1,594 patients; high certainty), trauma-related admission (aOR, 1.48; 95% CI, 0.93 to 2.34; three studies; 3,089 patients; high certainty), surgical-related admission (aOR, 2.50; 95% CI, 1.77 to 3.52; three studies; 2,208 patients; aHR, 1.35; 95% CI, 0.60 to 3.02; two studies; 297 patients; high certainty), internal jugular insertion site as compared with other insertion sites (aOR, 3.76; 95% CI, 2.82 to 5.01; four studies; 4,681 patients; high certainty), single/double-lumen as compared with more lumens (aOR, 1.61; 95% CI, 0.82 to 3.13; three studies; 1,594 patients; moderate certainty), and peripheral insertion site (aOR, 2.30; 95% CI, 0.74 to 7.08; two studies; 264 patients; moderate certainty). The median incidence of catheter-related thrombosis was 13.3% [interquartile range, 3.7%-31.3%].

CONCLUSIONS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we found that increasing age, surgical type admissions, large catheters, and factors potentially related with catheter duration were associated with developing a catheter-related thrombosis in the critical care setting. Furthermore, we identified significant variation in the reported rates of catheter-related thrombosis, with an average rate of approximately 1 in every 8 patients. When these identified risk factors are present, clinicians may consider more aggressive thromboprophylaxis regimens to better tailor prevention strategies to individual patient risk profiles.

Our secondary objective was to report the incidence of this entity. title: Impact of True and False Lumen Origins on Target Vessel Instability in Post-Dissection F/BEVAR.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the occurrence of target artery-related adverse events in post-dissection F/BEVAR patients, based upon artery origin from the true or false lumen.

METHODS: This is a multicenter, prospective, cohort study evaluating post-dissection patients treated with F/BEVAR, in the US Aortic Research Consortium. The primary endpoint was 5-year target vessel instability (TVI). Secondary endpoints included 5-year primary patency, freedom from secondary interventions (SIs), and type Ic and IIIc endoleaks. The analysis was performed on a per-vessel basis.

RESULTS: A total of 1052 target arteries were analyzed, primarily including the celiac, superior mesenteric, and renal arteries, with individual hepatic and splenic arteries occasionally incorporated in the repair. Of the 277 patients included, 75% were men, and 19% were black, with a mean age of 66.8 ± 10.3 years. The mean aneurysm sac diameter was 66.0 ± 11.4 mm, with extent II thoracoabdominal aneurysms being the most prevalent (72.6%) among this cohort. Technical success was obtained in 96% of the cases. As primary outcome, the incidence of target vessel instability (TVI) was significantly lower (P<0.001) among the true-lumen vessels (16.4%) compared to false-lumen (29.9%) and dual-lumen arteries (43.8%). As for the secondary outcomes, the incidence of type Ic endoleak was significantly higher (P=0.001) in false-lumen vessels (9.6%) and dual-lumen vessels (8.6%) compared to true-lumen vessels (3.3%). There was no significant difference in the incidence of type IIIc endoleak (p=0.241) or target vessel occlusion (P=0.458). Target artery stenosis was significantly more common among arteries originating from the false lumen compared to true lumen (2.6% vs 0.4%, P=0.009). Fenestrations were associated with a higher incidence (30.5%) of TVI when compared to branches (5.9% P=0.005), however, this was observed only among dual-lumen vessels. Arteries incorporated by a fenestration and that had a dual-lumen origin, were associated with a higher occurrence of secondary interventions (23.7%) compared to true-lumen vessels (8.6%, P=0.010). The same was not observed among the arteries incorporated by a branch configuration. The time-to-event analysis demonstrated a significantly higher 5-year freedom from TVI in true-lumen vessels compared to false and dual-lumen ones (True lumen: 83.6%; False=70.1 %; Dual=56.2 %; Log-rank P=0.0002). Freedom from secondary interventions at 5 years was significantly higher in true-lumen vessels compared to dual-lumen ones (Log-rank P=0.0104), but not to false-lumen arteries (Log-rank P=0.0847). The 5-year primary patency did not differ significantly among groups (True lumen: 98.3%; False = 92.6%; Dual=93.9%; Log-rank P=0.1368). On Cox proportional hazards analysis, dual-lumen (95% CI 1.24-3.28, p=0.005) and false-lumen (95% CI 1.04 - 2.60, p=0.0325) target arteries were associated with an increased hazard of TVI, when compared to true lumen arteries, having 2.02 (P=0.005) and 1.65 (P=0.0325) times more risk of presenting TVI than a true-lumen vessel CONCLUSIONS: In F/BEVAR for post-dissection aneurysms, target vessel instability and secondary intervention are significantly lower in target arteries originating from the true lumen, when compared to false-lumen or dual-lumen vessels. Device design, with use of fenestrations or branches may also play a role, with a significant difference only observed in dual-lumen target arteries.

METHODS: This is a multicenter, prospective, cohort study evaluating post-dissection patients treated with F/BEVAR, in the US Aortic Research Consortium. The primary endpoint was 5-year target vessel instability (TVI).

title: Lesion-targeting and vascular matrix-penetrating siRNA nanotherapeutics for the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract: Inefficient aneurysmal aorta enrichment and vascular matrix penetration represent major challenges against siRNA delivery for the management of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Herein, platelet membrane (PM)-reversibly camouflaged nanocomplexes (NCs) are developed to deliver Poldip2 siRNA (siPoldip2) into vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), which then restore vascular homeostasis by promoting phenotypic switching and mitigating oxidative stress. The NCs comprise a cationic nanocore assembled from siPoldip2 and a guanidinated and fluorinated bifunctional helical polypeptide (8FP), a charge-reversal intermediate layer of poly(l-lysine)-cis-aconitic acid (PC), and an outer shell of PM. After systemic administration in CaCl2-induced AAA rats, the NCs could preferentially accumulate at the aneurysmal site due to PM-mediated recognition of RGD-containing extracellular matrix proteins. The slightly acidic aneurysmal microenvironment subsequently triggers charge reversal of PC from negative to positive, which promotes the detachment of both PM and PC layers. The exposed 8FP/siPoldip2 nanocore penetrates the vascular matrix due to fluorocarbon-assisted repulsion of collagen mesh adsorption, followed by effective internalization by VSMCs. Consequently, Poldip2 expression in VSMCs is downregulated, which restores the contractile phenotype, and improves the aortic elasticity as well as structural integrity. This study provides a promising strategy for overcoming vascular delivery barriers and highlights the therapeutic promise of siRNA-based medical intervention for AAA.

The NCs comprise a cationic nanocore assembled from siPoldip2 and a guanidinated and fluorinated bifunctional helical polypeptide (8FP), a charge-reversal intermediate layer of poly(l-lysine)-cis-aconitic acid (PC), and an outer shell of PM.

title: Microsurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery and endovascular treatment of sylvian fissure arteriovenous malformations: a systematic review.
abstract: Sylvian-fissure-region arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are uncommon and anatomically heterogeneous; published labels often describe non-comparable lesions or populations. To update evidence for microsurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS), and endovascular treatment (EVT). Following PRISMA 2020, five databases were searched through May 2026 with citation chaining. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Dedicated sylvian/perisylvian cohorts were distinguished from broader cohorts and contextual technical reports. Incompatible endpoints, non-independent arms, and potentially overlapping cohorts were not pooled. Risk of bias and applicability were appraised. Nineteen reports were retained: 16 in the evidence synthesis and 3 as contextual background. Microsurgery achieved complete resection in 8/8, 40/41, and 94/94 patients. Transient deficits occurred in 4/8, 4/28, 9/94, and 18/41 patients; postoperative hematoma occurred in 2/94. Mortality windows varied. In the dedicated SRS cohort (n = 87), actuarial obliteration was 35% at 3 years, 60% at 4-5 years, and 76% at 10 years. Cumulative post-SRS hemorrhage was 5% at 1, 5, and 10 years (approximately 1% annually during latency); mortality was unreported. No dedicated curative EVT series for true sylvian AVMs was identified; available data described broader middle cerebral artery cohorts without sylvian-specific angiographic cure. Microsurgery is supported for carefully selected accessible sylvian-fissure AVMs, whereas SRS and embolization have complementary roles. Comparative superiority cannot be inferred. Future studies require explicit anatomical definitions, modality-specific denominators, angiographic endpoints, and standardized follow-up.

title: Incidence of Venous Thromboembolism After Elective Isolated Lumbar Decompression: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the reported incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and composite venous thromboembolism (VTE) after isolated lumbar decompression.

SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Prior VTE estimates often combine decompression-only procedures with more complex spine surgery, limiting procedure-specific risk estimation.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched on March 2, 2026, with surveillance through June 17, 2026. Decompression-only cohorts without fusion or instrumentation were eligible. Clinically detected, coded, or patient-reported outcomes were analyzed separately by event type and follow-up using random-effects binomial-normal generalized linear mixed models when at least five studies contributed data. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Twenty-five studies had a combined reported sample size of 831,732 patients. At 30 days, pooled DVT incidence was 0.283% (9 studies; 235,490 patients; 95% CI, 0.203%-0.393%) and PE incidence was 0.273% (7 studies; 235,341 patients; 95% CI, 0.171%-0.437%). At 90 days, DVT incidence was 0.225% (7 studies; 163,074 patients; 95% CI, 0.056%-0.905%) and PE incidence was 0.183% (6 studies; 162,772 patients; 95% CI, 0.041%-0.825%). Composite VTE estimates were heterogeneous. The low 30-day DVT and PE estimates persisted in leave-one-out analyses, while 90-day estimates were more sensitive to study inclusion. Only three studies reported chemical prophylaxis regimens. Different cohorts contributed to the two windows, which should not be interpreted as a temporal trend.

CONCLUSION: Reported 30-day DVT and PE incidences after isolated lumbar decompression were each approximately three events per 1,000 patients. These estimates provide a procedure-specific benchmark for counseling but do not establish the risk without prophylaxis or the effectiveness and overall benefit of chemoprophylaxis.
englishSummary: STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis. OBJECTIVE: To determine the reported incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and composite venous thromboembolism (VTE) after isolated lumbar decompression. SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Prior VTE estimates often combine decompression-only procedures with more complex spine surgery, limiting procedure-specific risk estimation.

title: Intravascular Ultrasound-Guided Emergency Endovascular Repair of a Tracheo-Innominate Artery Fistula for Severe Motor and Intellectual Disabilities.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tracheo-innominate artery fistula (TIF) is a lethal post-tracheostomy complication. In severe motor and intellectual disabilities, skeletal deformities and low surgical tolerance render open repair prohibitive, necessitating emergency hemostasis.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 31-year-old female with cerebral palsy developed massive tracheal hemorrhage 2 months post-tracheostomy. She presented with unstable vital signs, requiring manual syringe-push transfusion. Under cuff tamponade, emergency endovascular therapy (EVT) with Gore Viabahn and Viabahn VBX was chosen over open surgery due to thoracic deformities and limited time. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) localized the angiographically occult rupture site. Hemostasis was achieved, but suspected stent graft infection developed on Day 11 despite prophylactic antibiotic therapy. Following transition to comfort care, she died 27 days post-procedure due to anemia, hypotension, and impaired ventilation.

CONCLUSION: Emergency IVUS-guided EVT under cuff tamponade is a valuable life-saving strategy and potential definitive treatment option for TIF in patients with prohibitive surgical risk, though late-onset infection remains a critical challenge.

In severe motor and intellectual disabilities, skeletal deformities and low surgical tolerance render open repair prohibitive, necessitating emergency hemostasis. CASE PRESENTATION: A 31-year-old female with cerebral palsy developed massive tracheal hemorrhage 2 months post-tracheostomy.

title: Twenty-Year Forecast of Thoracic Surgeon Demand in Chile: Simulated Scenarios Using Bayesian Methods and Publicly Available Data.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Internationally, the thoracic surgery workforce is undergoing rapid changes due to increased training availability, particularly in Chile. There is currently no method for adequately forecasting the number of training spots needed to meet demand in future years.

METHODS: A national registry of thoracic surgeons was constructed using publicly available data from the Chilean Superintendency of Health (as of October 2024). Surgeons practicing cardiac or vascular surgery, retirees, and those living abroad were excluded. A Bayesian projection model was developed that incorporates parameters such as retirement age, entry of new surgeons (including graduates and foreign-certified individuals), accidental mortality, population growth, and dynamic demand growth. Monte Carlo simulations (1000 iterations) were conducted across five scenarios (1 to 5 graduates/year, plus one certified surgeon/year). Absolute error analysis identified the optimal annual number of new graduates.

RESULTS: Of the 107 thoracic surgeons listed in Chile, only 67 were actively practicing non-cardiac thoracic surgery. The majority were concentrated in the Metropolitan Region (capital). Sex distribution was predominantly male (83.5%), with a mean age of 50.2 years. The corrected model (using 67 active surgeons as the baseline) shows that a scenario with 1 graduate per year results in a projected shortage, while scenarios with 3-5 graduates per year lead to potential oversupply. The optimal scenario, minimizing supply-demand mismatch, was training approximately two to three surgeons per year (2.6 graduates/year).

CONCLUSIONS: Strategic workforce planning is essential to avoid future imbalances in thoracic surgeon availability. Bayesian modeling provides a robust framework for anticipating demand, guiding training capacity, and ensuring equitable distribution across regions, thereby avoiding both shortages and saturation of the specialty in Chile.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Internationally, the thoracic surgery workforce is undergoing rapid changes due to increased training availability, particularly in Chile. There is currently no method for adequately forecasting the number of training spots needed to meet demand in future years. METHODS: A national registry of thoracic surgeons was constructed using publicly available data from the Chilean Superintendency of Health (as of October 2024).

title: Risk Factors for Diabetic Foot-Related Lower Extremity Amputation in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot disease is a major cause of lower limb amputation (LLA) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where evidence on adjusted risk factors remains limited. This systematic review evaluates the risk factors for LLA and amputation-related mortality in diabetic foot disease across LMICs.

METHODS: Embase, MEDLINE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (via Ovid), PubMed, and Scopus were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies of adults with diabetes in LMICs reporting LLA with adjusted effect estimates were included. Pooling of effect estimates was prespecified to require at least three comparable studies per domain. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or AXIS.

RESULTS: Sixteen studies (19,529 participants; 1604 amputation events) provided usable effect estimates; 12 reported adjusted estimates from multivariable models. No domain contained three or more comparable estimates, so quantitative synthesis was not undertaken. Osteomyelitis was independently associated with amputation in both studies assessing it (aOR 5.60, 95% CI 2.93-10.78; aOR 11.8, 95% CI 5.1-27.5). Peripheral arterial disease was associated with LLA in two of three studies using objective vascular assessment (aOR 2.80, 95% CI 1.52-5.11; aOR 3.23 per grade, 95% CI 2.68-3.89). Prior amputation was associated with LLA in two DFU cohorts reporting concordant estimates (aOR 2.86 and 3.08). Ulcer severity was associated with amputation in every study assessing it, using five different classification systems. Prolonged ulcer duration carried an adjusted odds ratio of 10.3 (95% CI 4.06-26.13), and each additional preoperative day was associated with a 9.3% increase in the odds of major amputation. Neuropathy showed no independent association of meaningful size in any adjusted analysis, and HbA1c was not associated in the largest adjusted DFU cohort analysis, although a smaller study with 10 outcome events reported a positive association.

CONCLUSION: Peripheral arterial disease, ulcer severity, osteomyelitis, prior amputation, and delayed access to care were associated with LLA in LMIC settings. Neither neuropathy nor HbA1c showed an independent association of meaningful size in adjusted analyses of established DFU cohorts. Prospective LMIC cohorts using standardized definitions are needed.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot disease is a major cause of lower limb amputation (LLA) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where evidence on adjusted risk factors remains limited. This systematic review evaluates the risk factors for LLA and amputation-related mortality in diabetic foot disease across LMICs. METHODS: Embase, MEDLINE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (via Ovid), PubMed, and Scopus were searched from inception to March 2026.

title: A Ten-Year Single-Center Evaluation of In-Hospital Versus Seven- Versus Thirty-Day Outcomes as Quality Standards After Carotid Endarterectomy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) remains a cornerstone for stroke prevention. The 2023 European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guidelines recommend performing CEA only if the 30-day risk of stroke or death is < 3% for asymptomatic and < 6% for symptomatic patients. While clinical trials establish efficacy based on 30-day outcomes, reporting in-hospital complication rates offers greater feasibility in clinical routine. This study evaluates institutional compliance with ESVS thresholds and compares the reliability of in-hospital and 7-day outcomes versus the 30-day follow-up interval.

DESIGN: Retrospective single-center cohort study.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted at the Medical University of Graz, encompassing 2496 patients undergoing primary CEA between 2014 and 2023. Data were retrieved from the institutional information system and cross-referenced with national mortality registries (Statistik Austria) to ensure comprehensive follow-up. Primary endpoints included stroke and death within 7 and 30 days, stratified by symptomatic status and surgical technique-Eversion Endarterectomy (EEA) versus Conventional Endarterectomy (TEA) with patch angioplasty.

RESULTS: The final cohort comprised 2496 eligible procedures. Notably, a substantial proportion of events that occurred after hospital discharge, accounting for 17.9% (10/56) of all 30-day strokes and 60.0% (9/15) of all 30-day deaths were observed between hospital discharge and postoperative day 30. Overall, the in-hospital combined stroke and death rate was 1.5% for asymptomatic patients and 3.8% for symptomatic patients. Following discharge, additional events were recorded in 10 asymptomatic and 9 symptomatic patients, resulting in a cumulative 30-day combined stroke and death rate of 2.0% [95% CI: 1.4%-2.7%] for asymptomatic patients and 5.3% [95% CI: 3.5%-7.2%] for symptomatic patients, thereby meeting ESVS safety standards. While symptomatic status was a significant predictor of complications (p < 0.001), neither sex nor surgical technique (EEA vs. TEA-patch) exerted a significant influence on outcomes.

CONCLUSION: CEA is performed at ESVS-recommended safety levels in Graz. Contrasting a clinical tendency to favor more convenient in-hospital metrics, this study demonstrates that "in-hospital" data cannot be standardized due to highly variable discharge windows. Furthermore, while fixed 7-day complication rates provide a standardized timeline, they still significantly underestimate perioperative risks. The substantial rate of post-discharge perioperative strokes and deaths observed in our cohort underscores the clinical necessity of extending quality control to at least 30 days, which remains the superior metric for clinical audit.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) remains a cornerstone for stroke prevention. The 2023 European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guidelines recommend performing CEA only if the 30-day risk of stroke or death is < 3% for asymptomatic and < 6% for symptomatic patients. While clinical trials establish efficacy based on 30-day outcomes, reporting in-hospital complication rates offers greater feasibility in clinical routine.
