title: A 10-Year Single-Center Experience in Pediatric Thromboembolism: Management Strategies and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric thromboembolism is uncommon but clinically important, and its epidemiology varies according to age, underlying disease, catheter exposure, and referral patterns. This study evaluated the epidemiology, risk factors, management, and outcomes of pediatric thromboembolism over a 10-year period in a tertiary care center.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed children aged 0-18 years with symptomatic, radiologically confirmed thromboembolism between January 2010 and January 2020. Incidentally detected asymptomatic thromboses and cases without imaging confirmation were excluded. Venous and arterial events were analyzed separately.

RESULTS: Among 51,025 pediatric admissions, 70 patients had thromboembolism, corresponding to an admission-based rate of 13.7 per 10,000 admissions. Venous thromboembolism accounted for 51 cases (72.9%) and arterial thromboembolism for 19 cases (27.1%). Median age at diagnosis was 6 years (range, 1 day-18 years), and 49 patients (70.0%) were male. The central nervous system was the most frequent anatomical region involved. Central venous catheterization was the leading modifiable acquired risk factor. Active antithrombotic or interventional treatment was used in 68 patients (97.1%); low molecular weight heparin containing regimens were used in 46 patients (65.7%). Complete recovery was documented in 55 patients (78.6%), recurrence in 12 (17.1%), and mortality in 3 (4.3%). Recurrence was more frequent after venous than arterial events (23.5% vs 0%; p = .028).

CONCLUSION: In this 10-year cohort, venous events predominated and catheter related thrombosis remained a major preventable contributor. Recurrence was confined to venous events, supporting careful long term follow up and individualized secondary prevention for high risk children. Standardized catheter care practices and selective, appropriately timed thrombophilia testing are practical priorities.

This study evaluated the epidemiology, risk factors, management, and outcomes of pediatric thromboembolism over a 10-year period in a tertiary care center. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed children aged 0-18 years with symptomatic, radiologically confirmed thromboembolism between January 2010 and January 2020.

title: Situs Inversus Totalis with Mirror-Image Dextrocardia and Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Treated by Ascending Aorta Replacement Plus Total Arch Replacement and Frozen Elephant Trunk Using an Inverted Four-Branched Graft: A Case Report.
abstract: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital condition characterized by a complete mirror-image reversal of the thoracic and abdominal viscera, usually accompanied by dextrocardia. Acute type A aortic dissection (AAD) is a highly lethal cardiovascular emergency, and its coexistence with SIT is exceedingly rare. To the best of our knowledge, apart from a recently reported pregnant patient, no case of AAD in a non-pregnant adult with SIT has been treated with ascending aorta replacement combined with total arch replacement (TAR) and frozen elephant trunk (FET) implantation. In this report, we present such a case and share our surgical experience, particularly the inverted four-branched graft technique used to resolve the mismatch between the commercially available graft and the mirrored anatomy. The postoperative course was complicated by right renal malperfusion and stage 2 acute kidney injury. Overall renal function recovered with conservative management, although the right kidney subsequently became atrophic; otherwise, recovery was satisfactory. Computed tomographic angiography (CTA) at 10 months showed the graft and all reconstructed branches patent and the FET in position without endoleak, and the patient remained in good condition at the telephone follow-up approximately 3 years after surgery.
englishSummary: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital condition characterized by a complete mirror-image reversal of the thoracic and abdominal viscera, usually accompanied by dextrocardia. Acute type A aortic dissection (AAD) is a highly lethal cardiovascular emergency, and its coexistence with SIT is exceedingly rare. To the best of our knowledge, apart from a recently reported pregnant patient, no case of AAD in a non-pregnant adult with SIT has been treated with ascending aorta replacement combined with total arch replacement (TAR) and frozen elephant trunk (FET) implantation.

title: Snare-Assisted Traction Technique for Renal Artery Reconstruction in Endovascular Repair of Complex Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: Renal artery (RA) reconstruction during complex endovascular aortic repair often fails in hostile anatomy because of inadequate guidewire support. We describe snare-assisted traction (SAT), a novel endovascular bailout technique using conventional off-the-shelf devices. By combining distal snare traction with a long femoral sheath, SAT shifts target vessel reconstruction from simple wire guidance to sheath-based structural support. This provides robust stability for wire exchange and stent delivery without requiring specialized, unavailable tools or high-morbidity open conversion. Among 12 patients with severe RA angulation, ostial stenosis, or sac origin, SAT achieved 100% technical success without procedural complications. At median 6-month follow-up, all reconstructed RAs remained patent with stable renal function. SAT offers a safe, reproducible, and universally accessible solution for hostile target vessel access, significantly enhancing the feasibility and clinical safety of complex endovascular repair.

title: Venous thromboembolism after joint arthroplasty: where do we stand with aspirin?
abstract: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty remains heterogeneous, particularly regarding the role of aspirin within modern fast-track pathways. Although aspirin is widely used in North American arthroplasty practice, European guidelines remain more conservative and often provide limited or non-operational recommendations for its use after total hip and knee arthroplasty. Contemporary evidence supports aspirin as a viable prophylactic option in selected patients, with potential advantages related to its safety profile, cost, ease of administration and reduced treatment burden. The clinical role of aspirin should be interpreted within a risk-stratified framework that accounts for thromboembolic risk, bleeding risk, surgical complexity, early mobilization and duration of prophylaxis. Available evidence, including recent randomized data, supports aspirin-based prophylaxis in appropriately selected patients, both as part of sequential strategies and, increasingly, as monotherapy within contemporary fast-track pathways. This scoping review synthesizes current guideline-level evidence and contemporary clinical data to clarify practical considerations for agent selection, dosing, duration and aspirin-based prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty.

title: Reducing Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in ICUs: A Systematic Review of Barriers and Facilitators and Intervention Measures.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite established guidelines, central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) remains a severe ICU complication due to cognitive and resource barriers hindering healthcare worker compliance. A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention.

AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement.

STUDY DESIGN: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was performed using PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wan fang, and CBM databases, up to August 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods research on the barriers and facilitators to CLABSI prevention implementation among ICU healthcare workers. Two researchers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Data synthesis and intervention development were guided by the CFIR, with targeted strategies mapped using the CFIR-ERIC (Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change) matching tool.

RESULTS: The literature search identified 1,780 records, of which 28 studies were ultimately included. The review identified 28 barriers and facilitators, which were synthesized into four major themes and mapped to 16 CFIR constructs across the catheter-care continuum. The most prominent barriers involved staff knowledge gaps, inconsistent adherence to recommended practices, limited resources, and insufficient leadership support. CFIR-ERIC mapping identified 11 Level 1 expert-endorsed implementation strategies, of which four were represented in the included literature and seven were identified as potential implementation gaps.

CONCLUSIONS: CLABSI prevention in ICUs is influenced by multilevel implementation determinants spanning individual, organizational, and practice-related factors. A structured implementation-science approach may help healthcare organizations identify context-specific barriers and prioritize targeted strategies to support more consistent implementation of evidence-based CLABSI prevention practices.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Improving CLABSI prevention may require multilevel strategies that combine targeted education and training, adequate resource allocation, leadership engagement, standardized clinical procedures, and ongoing audit and feedback. These strategies may help strengthen adherence to evidence-based practices, improve quality of care, and enhance patient safety in ICUs.

AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement.

title: [From critical evaluation based on the gold standard to precision full-process management: advances in the diagnosis and treatment framework for aortic arch artery pathologies].
abstract: Supra-aortic arch artery diseases, including lesions of the carotid,subclavian,and vertebral arteries,represent major causes of cerebral and upper extremity ischemia. The diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for these conditions are undergoing a profound transformation-from conventional open surgery toward minimally invasive endovascular treatment,and further to individualized precision medicine. Recent advances in imaging assessment have substantially improved lesion characterization and risk stratification. The iterative evolution of endovascular devices has enhanced procedural safety. Meanwhile,several topics have become research hotspots,the evidence-based comparison between transcarotid artery revascularization and transfemoral carotid stenting;the renewed pathophysiological understanding of subclavian steal syndrome and vertebral artery diseases;and the construction of individualized treatment decision-making frameworks. Nevertheless,current clinical practice still faces challenges such as controversies over optimal surgical approaches,insufficient prevention and management of complications,and a lack of robust long-term outcome data. From the perspective of vascular surgery,this article systematically reviews recent advances in endovascular devices,surgical techniques,and treatment concepts,aiming to provide front-line clinicians with up-to-date,practical,and actionable insights into the management of supra-aortic arch artery diseases.

title: [A brief discussion on the progress and development directions of clinical research in vascular surgery].
abstract: Vascular surgery has experienced rapid development over the past three decades. With the application of minimally invasive and interventional techniques in the diagnosis and treatment of vascular diseases, clinical research and technological innovation in vascular surgery have expanded significantly. As populations aging accelerates globally-including in China-and the number of patients with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease within the existing healthcare system becomes increasingly evident. The future of vascular surgery will center on three core principles: minimization, precision, and intelligence. By integrating breakthroughs in basic science, engineering, and artificial intelligence, clinical translation will be accelerated. The discipline will shift from "disease treatment" to "health management", and from a "surgery-centered" single model to a "patient-centered" integrated approach model. Future developments will further incorporate artificial intelligence, big data models, precision medicine, more advanced and comprehensive minimally invasive technologies, enhancing multidisciplinary collaboration and preventive care. These advancements are expected to significantly improve diagnostic accuracy, treatment outcomes, and quality of life for patients with vascular diseases.

title: Mortality Following Recurrent Venous Thromboembolism and Major Bleeding Stratified by Active Cancer Status.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) and major bleeding are serious complications after acute VTE. However, their independent impact on subsequent mortality in the era of direct oral anticoagulants remains unclear, particularly with respect to differences between patients with and without active cancer.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the associations of recurrent VTE and major bleeding with subsequent mortality in the overall cohort and subgroups stratified by active cancer.

METHODS: We analyzed 5,197 patients with VTE from the COMMAND VTE Registry-2 using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models with recurrent VTE and major bleeding as time-updated covariates.

RESULTS: In the overall cohort, 283 patients developed recurrent VTE, 470 developed major bleeding, and 1,323 died. Recurrent VTE and major bleeding were associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 1.65, 95% CI: 1.28-2.12, P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 3.33, 95% CI: 2.83-3.91, P < 0.001, respectively). Among patients with active cancer, both recurrent VTE and major bleeding were associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 1.95, 95% CI: 1.45-2.62, P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 2.96, 95% CI: 2.42-3.61, P < 0.001, respectively). Among patients without active cancer, only major bleeding was associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 3.78, 95% CI: 2.88-4.97, P < 0.001), whereas recurrent VTE was not associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.55-1.56, P = 0.78).

CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary real-world patients with VTE in the era of direct oral anticoagulants, major bleeding was associated with increased subsequent mortality in both patients with and without active cancer, whereas recurrent VTE was associated with increased mortality in patients with active cancer, with no significant association observed in those without active cancer.

However, their independent impact on subsequent mortality in the era of direct oral anticoagulants remains unclear, particularly with respect to differences between patients with and without active cancer. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the associations of recurrent VTE and major bleeding with subsequent mortality in the overall cohort and subgroups stratified by active cancer.

title: Association of muscle strength with the incidence of venous thromboembolism and all-cause mortality among patients: a prospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Muscle strength is a well-established indicator of overall health, yet its prospective association with the incidence and prognosis of venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains inconsistent.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 481 945 participants without prior VTE from the UK Biobank for incidence analysis, and 14 908 patients with prevalent VTE at baseline for prognostic analysis. Muscle strength was assessed using grip strength relative to body weight and categorised into sex- and age-specific tertiles. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for incident VTE and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 13.72 years, 15 774 incident VTE events were documented. Each 1-standard deviation increase in muscle strength was associated with a 13% reduction in VTE risk (HR 0.87, 95% CI: 0.85-0.89). Compared with the low muscle strength group, participants in the middle and high tertiles had 12% (HR 0.88, 95% CI: 0.84-0.92) and 19% (HR 0.81, 95% CI: 0.77-0.84) lower risk of VTE. This inverse association remained consistent across all genetic risk strata. Among patients with VTE, 2884 deaths occurred during follow-up. Each 1-standard deviation increase was associated with a 14% lower mortality risk (HR 0.86, 95% CI: 0.82-0.90). High and middle muscle strength were associated with 21% (HR 0.79, 95% CI: 0.72-0.87) and 17% (HR 0.83, 95% CI: 0.76-0.91) lower all-cause mortality versus low strength.

CONCLUSION: Higher muscle strength is associated with a lower risk of incident VTE, regardless of genetic predisposition, and with lower mortality among patients with VTE.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 481 945 participants without prior VTE from the UK Biobank for incidence analysis, and 14 908 patients with prevalent VTE at baseline for prognostic analysis. Muscle strength was assessed using grip strength relative to body weight and categorised into sex- and age-specific tertiles.

title: Lesion-directed quantitative EEG after reperfusion therapy is associated with malignant cerebral edema and functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke: a prospective exploratory cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke causes electrophysiological slowing within minutes which may precede detectable structural changes, making electroencephalography (EEG) a sensitive bedside marker of tissue at risk. Prior quantitative EEG (qEEG) studies often averaged bilateral or frontal activity, focused on thrombectomy, and were recorded at 24 h. We tested whether a lesion-directed alpha-to-delta ratio (lesion-ADR) within 72 h after reperfusion is associated with malignant cerebral edema (MCE) and functional outcomes.

METHODS: In a prospective single-center cohort of anterior-circulation ischemic stroke treated with intravenous alteplase (IV-rtPA), endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), or both, a 7-min EEG was obtained ≤72 h after reperfusion. Lesion-ADR was defined as the mean ADR of ipsilesional electrodes; the reperfusion-to-EEG interval (ΔT) was recorded. The primary outcome was MCE (midline shift ≥5 mm and/or decompressive hemicraniectomy). Secondary outcomes were favorable functional outcomes at discharge and 90 days (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2). Model discrimination was assessed using ROC analysis and AUC with bootstrap internal validation. Adjusted associations were assessed using parsimonious Firth penalized logistic regression models.

RESULTS: Forty-nine patients were included. For MCE, the combined lesion-ADR + ΔT model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.888 (95% CI 0.765-0.960); bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.889. For discharge independence (mRS ≤ 2; n = 9), the ADR-only model showed an apparent AUC of 0.899. Lesion-ADR remained associated with favorable outcome after separate adjustment for admission NIHSS (OR 1.438 per 0.1-unit increase; p = 0.009) and reperfusion treatment modality (OR 1.367; p = 0.022). For 90-day independence (n = 13), the ADR-only AUC was 0.759 (95% CI 0.615-0.869) and the ADR-only model showed moderate discrimination for 90-day functional independence. The association with 90-day outcome was attenuated after accounting for admission NIHSS (OR 1.245 per 0.1-unit increase; p = 0.088).

CONCLUSION: A brief lesion-directed ADR obtained within 72 h after reperfusion was associated with functional outcomes, while its combination with EEG timing showed encouraging discrimination for MCE in this cohort. These exploratory findings suggest lesion-directed qEEG may serve as a potential adjunctive biomarker after reperfusion therapy and warrant validation in larger cohorts.

Prior quantitative EEG (qEEG) studies often averaged bilateral or frontal activity, focused on thrombectomy, and were recorded at 24 h. We tested whether a lesion-directed alpha-to-delta ratio (lesion-ADR) within 72 h after reperfusion is associated with malignant cerebral edema (MCE) and functional outcomes.

title: Chemical Mechanisms of Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury and Neuroprotection in the Thrombectomy Era.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has significantly improved outcomes for patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke. However, restoring the artery does not always re-establish full microvascular blood flow, tissue rescue, or a good neurological outcome. Ischemia-reperfusion injury varies over time, with distinct biochemical mechanisms dominating during ischemia, early reperfusion, and the subsequent hours. During ischemia, factors like adenosine triphosphate (ATP) depletion, ionic imbalance, calcium overload, mitochondrial dysfunction, acidosis, and metabolic changes such as succinate build-up render brain tissue highly vulnerable. When blood flow resumes, oxygen delivery to this stressed tissue can induce rapid mitochondrial redox shifts, electron leakage, reactive oxygen and nitrogen species formation, iron-dependent radical generation, and lipid peroxidation. Damage may then persist for hours through ongoing mitochondrial dysfunction, phospholipid hydroperoxide accumulation, reactive aldehydes, ferroptosis, blood-brain barrier breakdown, microvascular issues, and inflammation. Much of the mechanistic evidence supporting these processes derives from experimental studies, and their relevance to clinical outcomes after thrombectomy requires further validation. This narrative review tracks these chemical changes across the main phases of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury and connects them to modern thrombectomy practices. It also explores how the timing of each process may inform neuroprotective strategies, drug delivery methods, patient selection via imaging, and future clinical trial approaches.

However, restoring the artery does not always re-establish full microvascular blood flow, tissue rescue, or a good neurological outcome. Ischemia-reperfusion injury varies over time, with distinct biochemical mechanisms dominating during ischemia, early reperfusion, and the subsequent hours.

title: Precision medicine meets vascular disease: innovations in atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis management.
abstract: Atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis (ARAS) is a significant cause of secondary hypertension and kidney injury with important cardiovascular consequences. This review briefly discusses the pathophysiology of ARAS, evaluates in-depth the diagnostic performance of duplex ultrasound, computed tomography angiography, and magnetic resonance angiography, and synthesizes results from major randomized trials and observational studies to explore current treatment options. The objective is to define the current diagnostic and therapeutic landscape of ARAS in a manner that supports evidence-based clinical decision making, and identify which treatment modality may be appropriate based on clinical presentation. The preference for optimized medical therapy as the initial standard of care is largely based on multiple randomized controlled trials (RCTs), which found no overall benefit from invasive endovascular treatments in conjunction with medical therapy. However, the limitations in trial design indicate that these results do not rule out the benefit in carefully selected patients. Evidence from subgroup analyses and non-randomized studies supports invasive endovascular revascularization in presentations such as recurrent flash pulmonary edema, progressive decline in renal function, and hypertension resistant to pharmacologic medical therapy. Endovascular stenting is preferred when anatomy is favorable, while open surgical reconstruction, including aortorenal bypass or endarterectomy, is reserved for complex lesions, failed prior endovascular intervention, or concomitant aortic surgery. The review also discusses emerging strategies, including novel stent platforms and drug-eluting technology, which may improve outcomes if validated in targeted high-risk cohorts.

title: Major re-amputation after initial diabetic foot amputation: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Reamputation after initial diabetic foot amputation remains a major clinical challenge associated with substantial morbidity. Identifying factors related to major reamputation may improve patient management and limb preservation. This study evaluated the impact of clinical, metabolic, nutritional, and vascular parameters on the risk of major reamputation. This retrospective cohort study included 141 patients who underwent lower-extremity amputation for diabetic foot disease between 2020 and 2025. Demographic variables, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, peripheral arterial disease (PAD), infection history, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels, and Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) were analyzed. Major reamputation was defined as a subsequent ipsilateral amputation progressing to a below-knee or above-knee level; contralateral amputations and more proximal minor amputations confined to the foot were not considered outcome events. The median follow-up was 3.0 years (range, 1-5). Continuous variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test and categorical variables using the Pearson chi-square test. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate major reamputation-free survival, and Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to evaluate factors associated with time to major reamputation. A Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis was additionally performed considering death before major reamputation as a competing event. Major reamputation occurred in 31 patients (22.0%). Patients with reamputation had significantly lower BMI and PNI values and higher HbA1c levels (all P < .001). Smoking and PAD were significantly more frequent in the reamputation group (both P < .001), whereas no significant between-group differences were observed for age, sex, serum albumin, or infection history. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, PAD (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.25, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.13-18.32, P < .001) and higher HbA1c (adjusted HR 1.40, 95% CI 1.19-1.65, P < .001) were independently associated with an increased hazard of major reamputation, whereas higher PNI was associated with a reduced hazard (adjusted HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-0.99, P = .009). Lower BMI, higher HbA1c, reduced PNI, smoking, and PAD were associated with major reamputation. In multivariable time-to-event analysis, PAD, HbA1c, and PNI remained independently associated with the outcome. These findings demonstrate associations between routinely available clinical parameters and major reamputation and warrant further evaluation in prospective studies.

Identifying factors related to major reamputation may improve patient management and limb preservation. This study evaluated the impact of clinical, metabolic, nutritional, and vascular parameters on the risk of major reamputation.

title: Development and internal validation of machine-learning models for postoperative deep vein thrombosis after hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture: evaluation of Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome features.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains a clinically important complication after hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture. We evaluated whether Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) syndrome features add predictive information beyond conventional preoperative variables and examined the association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and postoperative DVT.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 380 patients. Group-constrained partitioning and resampling prevented identical prespecified multivariable profiles from crossing evaluation boundaries, yielding a development set (n = 267; 74 DVT events) and a profile-disjoint held-out validation set (n = 113; 31 events). Nine machine-learning algorithms were evaluated using a fixed eight-variable panel comprising D-dimer, fibrinogen, platelet count, type 2 diabetes, fasting blood glucose, TyG, Qi stagnation with blood stasis (QSBS), and Qi deficiency with blood stasis (QDBS). Random forest (RF) was selected on the basis of development-set out-of-fold performance before held-out validation.

RESULTS: Postoperative DVT occurred in 105 patients (27.6%). RF achieved a pooled group-aware development out-of-fold AUC of 0.774 (95% CI 0.710-0.837) and a held-out validation AUC of 0.859 (95% CI 0.782-0.935). Across 30 repeated group-constrained partitions, mean validation AUC was 0.792. In the single profile-disjoint held-out validation partition, the development-derived threshold of 0.298 yielded sensitivity of 0.903, specificity of 0.720, positive predictive value of 0.549, and negative predictive value of 0.952; in that same partition, the calibration slope was 1.136 (95% CI 0.753-1.867), the observed-to-expected ratio was 0.846, and the Brier score was 0.132. Adding QSBS and QDBS did not materially improve discrimination (AUC 0.855 vs. 0.859; ΔAUC = 0.003; DeLong p = 0.746). Higher TyG remained associated with DVT after multivariable adjustment (OR per 1 SD 1.550, 95% CI 1.186-2.026; p = 0.001); restricted cubic splines supported an overall association (p = 0.007) without significant evidence of nonlinearity (p = 0.082).

CONCLUSION: RF showed favorable discrimination in the held-out cohort but more modest performance across repeated group-constrained partitions. The two retained TCM syndrome variables did not provide a material increment in AUC, whereas higher TyG remained associated with postoperative DVT after multivariable adjustment. External validation and assessment of recalibration are required before clinical implementation.

We evaluated whether Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) syndrome features add predictive information beyond conventional preoperative variables and examined the association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and postoperative DVT. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 380 patients.

title: Serial computed tomography angiography-based computational fluid dynamics characterizes reduced near-renal tear exchange in kidneys that develop atrophy after aortic dissection repair.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal atrophy may develop after aortic dissection repair despite an anatomically patent renal artery on computed tomography angiography (CTA). This exploratory study compared serial near-renal aortic hemodynamics between kidneys with and without later renal-volume loss.

METHODS: Six index kidneys from six men were studied: three with ≥30% loss of reference volume (atrophy group) and three age-matched comparators. Patient-specific computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models were built from preoperative, early postoperative and late follow-up CTA; within each patient, inlet and outlet (three-element Windkessel) boundary conditions were identical across time points. All 90 true-lumen/false-lumen (TL/FL) communications were characterized by distance from the renal-ostial plane, direction, pressure difference and trans-tear flow. TL/FL relationships were quantified at the renal-ostial plane, and bilateral renal-artery flow was computed directly. Renal volume was measured by three-dimensional CTA segmentation.

RESULTS: All six index kidneys were supplied from the FL before repair. Index-kidney volume changed by -53.0%, -64.1% and -50.6% in the atrophy group and by -13.8%, +0.8% and -10.7% in comparators. No hemodynamic measure separated the groups before repair. From the early postoperative model onward (3-37 days), two aortic-level flow measures were lower in every atrophy kidney than in every comparator: the FL flow-magnitude fraction at the renal-ostial plane (0.03-0.10 versus 0.13-0.79) and total peak-systolic trans-communication flow (37.8-45.1 versus 61.8-185.3 mL/s). Index renal-artery flow separated the groups only at late follow-up (-29.4%, -32.6% and -63.9% versus +5.9%, -7.4% and -3.0%), as did tear-exchange flow directed toward the renal-ostial level (1.9-19.1 versus 38.7-130.9 mL/s). FL/TL pressure ratios did not separate the groups at any time point. In one patient-derived geometry, sequential virtual closure of idealized communications redistributed and reversed flow in the remaining communications; index renal-artery flow after the final closure was similar to baseline.

CONCLUSION: In kidneys that later atrophied, the FL flow contribution at the renal level was lower than in comparators early after repair, before the modeled decrease in renal-artery flow and, in two of three kidneys, before substantial volume loss. Given three kidneys per group and multiple measures, these associations are hypothesis-generating and do not establish causation, renal parenchymal perfusion or a treatment threshold.

This exploratory study compared serial near-renal aortic hemodynamics between kidneys with and without later renal-volume loss. METHODS: Six index kidneys from six men were studied: three with ≥30% loss of reference volume (atrophy group) and three age-matched comparators.

title: Prognostic performance of the WIfI classification in diabetic patients with infrapopliteal CLTI after endovascular revascularization: a subgroup analysis of the PRIME-WIFI registry.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) classification is widely used in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, its prognostic performance in diabetic patients after endovascular revascularization remains unclear. We evaluated its prognostic and discriminatory performance in this population.

METHODS: This subgroup analysis of the prospective, multicenter PRIME-WIFI registry included diabetic patients with infrapopliteal CLTI undergoing endovascular revascularization. Associations between baseline WIfI stage and MAE (all-cause mortality, major amputation, or clinically driven target-limb reintervention), its individual components, amputation-free survival, clinical improvement, and 12-month VascuQoL change were assessed using Kaplan-Meier, multivariable Cox, and Harrell's C-index analyses.

RESULTS: A total of 707 diabetic patients (730 limbs) were analyzed; in the full PRIME-WIFI cohort, diabetes status showed a borderline interaction with WIfI stage for MAE (P for interaction = 0.083). One-year freedom from MAE decreased across WIfI stages (89.5%, 77.4%, 78.0%, and 70.1% for stages 1-4; log-rank P = 0.004), and WIfI stage independently predicted MAE (HR: 1.31; 95% CI: 1.09-1.56; P = 0.0031). One-year AFS was 94.7%, 83.3%, 83.3%, and 74.2% (log-rank P = 0.0003), with higher WIfI stage associated with worse AFS (HR: 1.53; 95% CI: 1.24-1.89; P < 0.001). Overall survival was 94.7%, 87.8%, 86.1%, and 80.3% (log-rank P = 0.009), and WIfI stage was independently associated with mortality (HR: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.20-1.94; P < 0.001). Freedom from major amputation was 100.0%, 95.3%, 96.8%, and 92.3% (log-rank P = 0.02), with higher WIfI stage independently associated with major amputation (HR: 1.62; 95% CI: 1.07-2.57; P = 0.020). In contrast, freedom from CD-TLR did not differ significantly across stages (log-rank P = 0.60; HR: 0.92; 95% CI: 0.68-1.23; P = 0.564). Clinical improvement tended to decrease with increasing WIfI stage but did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.053). VascuQoL scores improved from baseline to 12 months across all WIfI stages, with no significant difference in the magnitude of improvement among stages (time-by-WIfI interaction P = 0.247).

CONCLUSIONS: In this diabetic subgroup, WIfI retained prognostic value for MAE, AFS, mortality, and major amputation. However, discrimination was clearest between stages 1 and 4, with limited separation between stages 2 and 3. These findings support WIfI for broad risk stratification while highlighting the need for complementary assessment in diabetic CLTI.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: The Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) classification is widely used in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, its prognostic performance in diabetic patients after endovascular revascularization remains unclear. We evaluated its prognostic and discriminatory performance in this population.

title: Effect of a Nurse-Driven Early Mobilization Protocol on Biomarker Levels and Incidence of Deep Vein Thrombosis After Lower Extremity Fracture Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a nurse-driven early mobilization protocol on the incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), biomarker levels, and clinical outcomes in patients after lower extremity fracture surgery.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 205 patients who underwent surgery for traumatic unilateral lower extremity fractures (January 2023 to June 2025). Patients were divided into a control group (conventional care, n = 107) and an early mobilization group (nurse-driven protocol, n = 98) using July 2024 as the implementation cutoff. Outcomes included postoperative DVT incidence, changes in D-dimer and C-reactive protein (CRP), bed rest duration, pain scores, length of stay, and complications. Repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) compared biomarker changes; binary logistic regression identified DVT risk factors.

RESULTS: The early mobilization group had a significantly lower incidence of postoperative DVT than the control group (7.14% vs. 19.63%, P = 0.009), with an absolute risk reduction of 12.49% and a relative risk reduction of 63.6%. Repeated-measures ANOVA showed significant between-group effects (F = 22.33, P < 0.001) and interaction effects (F = 6.36, P < 0.001) for CRP levels. After Bonferroni correction, the early mobilization group had significantly lower D-dimer and CRP levels at 1 week postoperatively and at discharge than the control group (P < 0.0125). The early mobilization group also had significantly better outcomes in terms of bed rest duration (5.86 ± 1.69 days vs. 6.38 ± 1.54 days, P = 0.021), numerical rating scale score on postoperative day 3 (3.27 ± 1.15 vs. 4.54 ± 1.47, P < 0.001), and length of hospital stay (median 11.00 days vs. 13.00 days, P < 0.001), as well as a lower complication rate (6.12% vs. 14.95%, P = 0.041). Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified the early mobilization protocol (odds ratio [OR] = 0.27, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.10-0.73, P = 0.009), age (OR = 1.05, 95% CI: 1.02-1.08, P = 0.001), and postoperative day 1 D-dimer level (OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.05-1.47, P = 0.011) as independent factors influencing postoperative DVT.

CONCLUSION: A nurse-driven early mobilization protocol effectively reduces the incidence of DVT after lower extremity fracture surgery, improves coagulation and inflammatory biomarker levels, shortens hospital stay, and does not increase complication risks. The protocol is safe and feasible and can be recommended as an adjunctive measure for venous thromboembolism prevention after lower extremity fracture surgery.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 205 patients who underwent surgery for traumatic unilateral lower extremity fractures (January 2023 to June 2025). Patients were divided into a control group (conventional care, n = 107) and an early mobilization group (nurse-driven protocol, n = 98) using July 2024 as the implementation cutoff.

title: Do Preoperative Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Influence Lumbar Fusion Outcomes? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly used in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, but lumbar fusion-specific associations with postoperative outcomes remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between preoperative GLP-1RA exposure and surgical and postoperative outcomes in adults undergoing lumbar fusion.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through 14 May 2026. Comparative studies of adults undergoing lumbar fusion with and without preoperative GLP-1RA exposure were included. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I). Random-effects meta-analyses generated odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261414637).

RESULTS: Seven retrospective cohorts involving 28,525 patients were included; 6 used propensity score matching or another matching strategy. No statistically significant associations were observed between preoperative GLP-1RA exposure and reoperation or revision (OR: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.44-1.24; P = 0.25), postoperative infection (OR: 0.83, 95% CI: 0.68-1.00; P = 0.05), wound complications (OR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.65-1.12; P = 0.26), or postoperative respiratory complications (OR: 1.08, 95% CI: 0.63-1.84; P = 0.69). Deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and unplanned emergency department visits also did not differ significantly. All included studies were observational and predominantly used large administrative data sources.

CONCLUSIONS: Across the evaluated outcomes, the available observational evidence did not identify a signal of increased postoperative risk associated with preoperative GLP-1RA exposure after lumbar fusion. Prospective studies with standardized exposure definitions and perioperative management protocols are warranted to confirm these findings and better define their clinical implications.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current observational evidence does not establish preoperative GLP-1RA exposure alone as an independent risk factor for adverse outcomes after lumbar fusion.

title: Association of circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography with preoperative rupture in type A aortic dissection.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography (CTA) and preoperative rupture in patients with type A aortic dissection (TAAD).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 597 consecutive patients diagnosed with TAAD at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Patients were classified into circumferential dissection (n = 130) and non-circumferential dissection (n = 467) groups based on preoperative CTA. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging characteristics were compared between groups. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to examine factors independently associated with preoperative rupture, and between-group differences in preoperative rupture were compared.

RESULTS: Circumferential dissection was strongly associated with DeBakey type I dissection, supra-aortic branch involvement, and greater false-lumen expansion with true-lumen compression. Preoperative rupture occurred more frequently in patients with circumferential dissection than in those without (33.8% vs 7.1%, P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that circumferential dissection was independently associated with preoperative rupture ascertained by bedside echocardiography following the admission CTA after adjustment for demographic, laboratory, and imaging factors (OR = 5.24, 95% CI: 1.86-14.76, P = 0.002).

CONCLUSION: Circumferential dissection on CTA is independently associated with preoperative rupture and may support timely surgical decision-making in TAAD.

title: Use and Safety of Peripherally Inserted Venous Catheters Versus Central Venous Catheters for Patients With Lymphoma Receiving Frontline Anthracycline-based Chemotherapy.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Peripheral intravenous catheters (PIVs) for the administration of anthracycline-based chemotherapy have the potential risk of vascular and tissue injury due to extravasation of vesicant agents. Central venous catheters (CVCs) are frequently utilized to mitigate this. This multicenter retrospective real-world analysis (RWA) evaluated complications associated with PIVs versus CVCs for the administration of anthracycline-based chemotherapy in patients with lymphoma.

METHODS: We conducted a RWA across 9 US medical centers, including adults with newly diagnosed lymphoma who received anthracycline-based chemotherapy via PIV or CVC between 2010 and 2025. Detailed baseline characteristics and safety outcomes were collected, applying standard definitions for extravasation and other recognized complications. Incidence rates of safety outcomes were calculated, and multivariable Poisson regression models were applied to adjust for confounders.

RESULTS: In total, 1776 patients were included: 1077 with CVCs, 886 with PIVs, and 187 with both. The most common diagnoses were large B-cell lymphomas, followed by Hodgkin lymphoma, and then T-cell lymphoma. In total, there were 5464 and 4049 treatment cycles in the CVC and PIV cohorts, respectively. There was one definite case of extravasation with PIV use (incidence rate 0.19 events per 1000 infusion-cycles), compared to no cases with CVC use. PIV use was more commonly associated with flare, phlebitis, and pain, whereas CVC use was more commonly associated with deep vein thrombosis; other complications were not different between cohorts. Rates of extravasation and other complications were low in both PIV and CVC cohorts.

CONCLUSION: Altogether, PIVs represent a viable modality for patients with lymphoma requiring anthracycline-based chemotherapy.

Central venous catheters (CVCs) are frequently utilized to mitigate this. This multicenter retrospective real-world analysis (RWA) evaluated complications associated with PIVs versus CVCs for the administration of anthracycline-based chemotherapy in patients with lymphoma.

title: Machine learning assisted thermal reperfusion mapping reveals real-time changes in foot microcirculation during endovascular revascularisation.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To test the feasibility of a novel thermal perfusion imaging and mapping system to show microcirculatory changes of plantar foot angiosomes during endovascular procedures.

METHODS: A prospective, exploratory MedTech development study was designed to test the system in a series of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI). Intraprocedural video thermography was performed using a 320 × 240 pixel resolution, thermal camera. Initial analysis was manual, re- positioning regions of interest (ROIs) within each of five plantar foot angiosomes. Subsequent automation using deep learning segmentation allowed ROI tracking from initial frame to procedure end. Isotherms (thermal contours) created and applied to the segmented surface provide quantitative, real-time changes in the percentage distribution of isotherms overlying both treated and contralateral foot angiosomes during the procedure.

RESULTS: Of 23 participants recruited, video thermography was obtained in 21 patients admitted with moderate-severe disease complexity; femoral-popliteal segment only (n = 13), femoral-popliteal and infrapopliteal disease (n = 5) and infrapopliteal disease only (n = 3). Changes in percentage distribution of each isotherm overlay revealed two broad groups; plantar foot thermal perfusion responders (n = 12) and non-responders (n = 9). In responders, revascularisation led to a series of 'dynamic' phases where temperature increased in one, or more, angiosomes; 'hottest' isotherms expanded significantly (p = .002) in response to endovascular procedures. In thermal perfusion non-responders, no significant change in isotherm percentage distribution was observed.

CONCLUSION: Thermal perfusion imaging is feasible using the novel implemented deep learning system. Clinicians can gain insight about microcirculatory changes at foot angiosomes in response to treatment based on three parameters; (i) temporal temperature profiles of each angiosome, (ii) real-time changes in the percentage distribution of isotherms across the plantar surface during the intervention, (iii) angiosome-specific cutaneous perfusion responses to balloon inflation and/or stent deployment. For patients with diabetes, locating the site of improved skin reperfusion has potential to predict treatment success for healing outcomes at the ulcer/woundosome.

METHODS: A prospective, exploratory MedTech development study was designed to test the system in a series of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI). Intraprocedural video thermography was performed using a 320 × 240 pixel resolution, thermal camera.

title: Development of a multidisciplinary service-delivery framework for venous thromboembolism prevention in hospitalized medical patients with lung cancer: a mixed-methods modified Delphi study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a common and potentially preventable complication in patients with lung cancer. Although clinical guidelines recommend risk assessment and appropriate prophylaxis, hospitals often lack operational frameworks for translating these recommendations into multidisciplinary workflows, quality monitoring, and continuous improvement. This study aimed to develop a hospital-based multidisciplinary service-delivery framework for VTE prevention and management among hospitalized medical patients with lung cancer.

METHODS: A mixed-methods modified Delphi study was conducted. Candidate framework items were generated from a structured literature review and semi-structured interviews with physicians, nurses, clinical pharmacists, and hospital managers, and were organized using Donabedian's Structure-Process-Outcome model. A two-round Delphi survey was then conducted with 15 experts from respiratory medicine, oncology, clinical pharmacy, nursing management, and hospital quality management. Experts rated the importance and feasibility of each candidate item, and the framework was refined using predefined consensus criteria and qualitative feedback.

RESULTS: The response rate was 100% in both Delphi rounds. Expert authority coefficients were 0.943 and 0.953 in rounds 1 and 2, respectively. Kendall's W ranged from 0.249 to 0.292, indicating low-to-moderate concordance despite statistically significant tests. The final framework included 3 first-level domains, 11 second-level components, and 34 third-level indicators covering structural capacity, care processes, and outcome monitoring. Importance ratings were generally higher than feasibility ratings, particularly for indicators requiring information system support, multidisciplinary coordination, and post-discharge continuity of care.

CONCLUSION: This study developed a preliminary, consensus-based multidisciplinary service-delivery framework for hospital-based VTE prevention in patients with lung cancer. The framework may support the operationalization of guideline recommendations, standardization of care processes, and prioritization of quality improvement efforts. Prospective implementation studies are needed to evaluate its feasibility, transferability, and impact on care quality and patient outcomes.

Although clinical guidelines recommend risk assessment and appropriate prophylaxis, hospitals often lack operational frameworks for translating these recommendations into multidisciplinary workflows, quality monitoring, and continuous improvement. This study aimed to develop a hospital-based multidisciplinary service-delivery framework for VTE prevention and management among hospitalized medical patients with lung cancer.

title: Emergent or urgent hybrid repair for complex thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms: single-centre experience.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Emergent or urgent repair of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA) always represent a major challenge due to high mortality and complex reconstruction of visceral arteries. We aimed to evaluate the short- and long-term outcomes of patients undergoing emergent or urgent hybrid TAAA repair under a standardized institutional perioperative protocol.

METHODS: This study represents a retrospective cohort analysis of data derived from a prospectively maintained institutional database at West China Hospital. All consecutive patients who underwent emergent or urgent hybrid repair for TAAA between January 2013 and February 2025 were included.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 38 TAAA patients (31 male, with a median age of 50.5 years) who underwent emergent/urgent hybrid repair. The median aneurysm length was 200.9 mm (IQR 154.0-320.0), with a mean maximum diameter was 70.5 ± 17.8 mm. Intraoperatively, 4 visceral arteries (IQR 4-5) were reconstructed. Median operative time was 415 min (IQR 360-504), with median ICU and postoperative hospital stays of 96.0 h (IQR 46.5-203.5) and 17 days (IQR 11-24), respectively. No myocardial infarction or hepatic failure occurred. Postoperative complications included pulmonary infection (n = 4, 10.5%), acute kidney injury (n = 2, 5.3%), and spinal cord ischemia (n = 5, 13.2%). Thirty-day mortality was 10.5% (n = 4). The survival rates at 12 and 60 months postoperatively were 86.8% (95% CI 76.7-98.3) and 83.0% (95% CI 71.7-96.6). The free of reintervention rates at 12 and 60 months postoperatively were 90.5% (95% CI 80.8-100.0) and 76.4% (95% CI 61.1-95.7).

CONCLUSION: In this selected cohort managed with a standardized perioperative protocol, emergent and urgent hybrid TAAA repair was feasible, with acceptable perioperative mortality and durable mid- to long-term survival. However, the occurrence of spinal cord ischemia represents a substantial and clinically significant trade-off of this approach in the emergency setting. Moreover, these favorable survival outcomes should be interpreted in the context of the cohort's relatively young age and favorable baseline risk profile. These findings emphasize that survival benefit is counterbalanced by significant neurological morbidity, highlighting the need for refined spinal protection protocols in urgent cases and for comparative studies to validate the specific efficacy of this standardized protocol.

title: One-Year Sac Regression after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair Is Not Always Associated with Favorable Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: It is not clear whether 1-year sac regression after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) indicates the completion of treatment. The purpose of our study is to identify the association between 1-year sac behaviors and clinical outcomes and specifically whether it is safe to extend follow-up intervals for patients with 1-year sac regression.

METHODS: This is a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 317 consecutive patients who underwent nonruptured EVAR from January 2011 to December 2020. All patients were stratified into three groups based on their 1-year sac behavior: sac regression (decrease in diameter of ≥ 5 mm), stable sac (<5 mm change), and sac expansion (increase in diameter of ≥ 5 mm). The primary outcome was late reintervention, including endovascular reintervention and open conversion (OC).

RESULTS: A total of 317 patients were enrolled based on sac status on 1-year follow-up imaging: 126 with sac regression, 177 with stable sacs, and 14 with sac expansion. Over a median follow up of 69.5 months, sac expansion was a significant risk factor for late reintervention compared to sac regression (hazard ratio [HR], 2.335; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.048-5.191; P = 0.047). However, the rate of late reintervention was not significantly lower in the sac regression group compared to the stable sac group (HR, 0.694; 95% CI, 0.383-1.258; P = 0.229). Among patients with sac regression at 1 year, 5.6% (7/126) required embolization due to endoleak (EL), and 3.2% (4/126) needed OCs.

CONCLUSION: Late reintervention rates did not differ significantly between patients with stable versus regressed sacs at 1 year. Patients with sac regression also require regular imaging surveillance to detect late complications.

METHODS: This is a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 317 consecutive patients who underwent nonruptured EVAR from January 2011 to December 2020.

title: Early Morphological Changes in Superficial Varicose Veins after Endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To quantify early changes in untreated varicose tributaries and treated saphenous veins after isolated radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and to assess 3-month technical outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 133 patients undergoing RFA of the great saphenous vein (GSV; n = 120) or small saphenous vein (SSV; n = 13). The primary outcome was within-patient change in the largest untreated varicose tributary diameter from baseline to approximately 3 months. The same radiologist reassessed the anatomically documented site. We used paired analyses, bootstrap confidence intervals, and multivariable analysis of covariance with robust standard errors.

RESULTS: Median tributary diameter decreased from 14.2 mm (interquartile range [IQR], 10.5-21.0) to 11.0 mm (IQR, 7.4-14.2). The median within-patient reduction was 3.0 mm (IQR, 0.9-5.8; 95% bootstrap confidence interval [CI], 2.2-3.7; P < 0.001). Completion duplex ultrasonography (DUS) confirmed closure of the proximal treated saphenous segment and patency of the adjacent deep vein in all patients. At approximately 3 months, complete occlusion was present in 99 of 120 GSVs (82.5%) and all 13 SSVs. The remaining 21 GSVs had short-segment partial recanalization with residual reflux near the saphenofemoral junction; none had complete recanalization. In an exploratory adjusted analysis, diabetes mellitus was associated with a 1.15-mm larger 3-month GSV diameter (95% CI, 0.23-2.07; P = 0.015).

CONCLUSION: Isolated RFA was associated with an early reduction in untreated varicose tributary diameter. These anatomical findings suggest that reassessment before adjunctive tributary treatment may be reasonable; however, clinical benefit cannot be inferred without patient-reported outcomes. The association between diabetes and 3-month GSV diameter is hypothesis-generating.

The primary outcome was within-patient change in the largest untreated varicose tributary diameter from baseline to approximately 3 months.

title: From Receptor Architecture to Outcome Maturity: A Clinical Framework for Multiorgan Incretin Therapy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To propose a clinically usable framework that separates receptor architecture and metabolic potency from the maturity of patient-relevant outcome evidence for incretin-based therapies.

METHODS: This Commentary draws on recent cardiovascular, kidney, heart failure, peripheral artery disease, liver, and emerging polyagonist evidence to define outcome maturity across 5 domains: endpoint directness and clinical relevance; study design and evidentiary confidence; comparator and population context; follow-up duration, durability, and safety; and molecule-, dose-, and indication-specific applicability.

RESULTS: Four qualitative states of outcome evidence are proposed: preliminary, emerging, established, and mature. These categories apply to a specific molecule, dose, indication, phenotype, and outcome question and are intentionally nonnumeric. Outcome maturity does not measure treatment-effect magnitude or comparative drug efficacy. A six-step clinical workflow links the dominant organ-risk phenotype, clinically meaningful outcome, evidence maturity, applicability, treatment sustainability, and proportionate clinical positioning.

CONCLUSION: Receptor architecture defines biological potential, whereas outcome maturity characterizes the directness, robustness, durability, and applicability of clinical evidence. Clinical positioning should remain proportional to phenotype-specific evidence and should not convert differences between nonaligned trials into cross-trial efficacy rankings.

RESULTS: Four qualitative states of outcome evidence are proposed: preliminary, emerging, established, and mature.

title: The Need for Device-Specific Training Before Handheld Ultrasound Use: Agreement and Repeatability of Simulated Aortic Aneurysm Diameter Measurements by Senior Sonography Students on a Familiar Conventional and an Unfamiliar Handheld System.
abstract: Background: Ultrasound measurement of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) diameter guides screening and surveillance, but whether students' measurement competence on a conventional system transfers to an unfamiliar handheld device has rarely been assessed. Methods: Twenty-seven senior sonography students made three anteroposterior outer-to-outer measurements of two water-filled balloons embedded in gelatin (reference diameters 3.53 and 5.88 cm, calculated from the circumference before embedding), first on the familiar cart-based conventional system and then, in a fixed, non-randomised order, on a handheld system with which they had no prior hands-on experience. The primary outcomes were bias against the calculated reference, with equivalence testing (±5%), and the paired between-system difference, with Bland-Altman analysis; repeatability was assessed with repeatability coefficients. Results: Conventional measurements were equivalent to the calculated reference within ±5% (bias -0.09 cm, 95% CI -0.16 to -0.02; +0.07 cm, 95% CI -0.05 to +0.19). Handheld measurements were higher (+0.17 and +0.33 cm; both p < 0.001) and failed equivalence; the mean between-system difference was +0.26 cm (95% CI 0.18-0.34), without proportional bias. Single-reading repeatability coefficients were 0.31-0.67 cm. Conclusions: Students' conventional-system measurements agreed closely with the calculated reference, although this reference was not verified after embedding. Because device type was confounded with operator inexperience and with a fixed testing order, which introduces an unquantifiable learning or fatigue effect, the 0.26 cm value is an observed between-system difference under the study conditions and cannot be attributed to the handheld device itself. Measurement competence did not transfer automatically to a new device, underlining the critical need for device-specific training before handheld systems are used for aortic measurement. These implications are educational and technical; phantom findings do not support clinical surveillance recommendations without confirmation in patients.

title: Multimodal integration of carotid plaque ultrasound radiomics and dynamic systemic immune-inflammation trajectories for subacute risk stratification after stroke thrombectomy: development and internal validation of an exploratory prognostic model.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We hypothesized that integrating macroscopic carotid plaque architecture, quantified via ultrasound radiomics, with downstream micro-cellular temporal dynamics, defined by longitudinal immune trajectories, would yield a highly accurate prognostic framework for 90-day functional outcomes in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT).

METHODS: This single-center, retrospective cohort study consecutively included 316 AIS-LVO patients who underwent successful EVT (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2b) within 24 h of symptom onset. Patients were partitioned into a discovery (N = 221) and an internal validation cohort (N = 95) using stratified random sampling. To capture temporal inflammatory heterogeneity, the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) was measured at days 0, 1, 3, and 7, and clustered using Latent Class Mixed Models (LCMM). Concurrently, high-dimensional radiomic features strictly adhering to the Image Biomarker Standardisation Initiative (IBSI) guidelines were extracted from baseline two-dimensional carotid ultrasound images. A radiomics score (Rad-score) was constructed utilizing Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression. Four progressive predictive models were developed, culminating in an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) multimodal architecture. The primary endpoint was an unfavorable 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 3 to 6).

RESULTS: An unfavorable outcome occurred in 166 of 316 patients (52.5%). The LCMM objectively identified three longitudinal SII phenotypes. The "persistent high-inflammation" trajectory (Class 3, 17.0% of patients) was independently associated with an increased risk of an unfavorable outcome compared to the "rapid resolution" trajectory (Class 1) [adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 4.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.20 to 10.85; p < 0.001]. The ultrasound Rad-score, comprising 9 core textural features, also demonstrated robust independent predictive value (aOR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.21 to 1.92 per 0.1-point increase; p < 0.001). In the strictly isolated internal validation cohort, the full multimodal XGBoost model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86 to 0.97), with an accuracy of 86.3%, sensitivity of 88.0%, and specificity of 84.4%. This performance was statistically superior to the standard clinical baseline model (AUC, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.63 to 0.84; p < 0.001 via DeLong test). Furthermore, the multimodal paradigm demonstrated clinical reclassification utility, yielding a continuous net reclassification improvement of 0.985 (95% CI, 0.684 to 1.286) and an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.194 (95% CI, 0.128 to 0.260).

CONCLUSION: An exploratory model integrating baseline carotid plaque ultrasound radiomics with Day-0-to-Day-7 systemic immune-inflammation trajectories was associated with 90-day functional outcome after EVT and, on internal validation, discriminated outcomes more strongly than a conventional clinical model. Because the immune-trajectory component is only complete at Day 7, the model is intended for subacute post-EVT risk stratification rather than acute treatment selection, and requires external, prospective validation before any clinical application.

METHODS: This single-center, retrospective cohort study consecutively included 316 AIS-LVO patients who underwent successful EVT (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2b) within 24 h of symptom onset. Patients were partitioned into a discovery (N = 221) and an internal validation cohort (N = 95) using stratified random sampling.

title: Inflammation-associated clinical prognostic factors and primary patency after drug-coated balloon angioplasty for recurrent autogenous arteriovenous fistula stenosis: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) stenosis occurs in a vascular environment in which injury, neointimal hyperplasia and inflammation may coexist. Whether routine inflammatory or hematological markers contribute to clinical prognosis after drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty remains uncertain. This retrospective study examines clinical outcomes and inflammation-related prognostic associations without assuming that inflammatory pathways were measured or causally established.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort comprised 357 patients treated between February 2023 and May 2026. The primary outcome was time from index DCB angioplasty to clinically driven target-lesion reintervention. Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses used available follow-up; a separate clinical logistic model addressed failure within 12 months in 356 patients with complete model data. No non-DCB comparator or patient-level molecular measurements were available.

RESULTS: Mean brachial-artery flow increased from 288.98 ± 139.37 to 980.92 ± 174.66 mL/min and minimal luminal diameter from 1.52 ± 0.50 to 5.21 ± 0.63 mm (both P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier primary patency was 95.24%, 84.03%, 68.90%, and 55.40% at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. In the extended Cox model (338 patients; 191 events), previous PTA count (HR 1.129 per procedure, P = 0.003) and lesion length (HR 1.105 per cm, P = 0.001) were associated with greater hazard; postprocedural flow (HR 0.889 per 100 mL/min, P = 0.014) and red-blood-cell count (HR 0.804 per 1012/L, P = 0.027) were associated with lower hazard. The five-fold cross-validated AUC of the clinical 12-month model was 0.706.

CONCLUSION: In this selected single-center cohort, recurrent AVF stenosis after DCB angioplasty was associated with previous PTA burden, lesion length, postprocedural flow, and red-blood-cell count. Routine blood-cell measures provide an exploratory inflammation-related clinical context but do not establish inflammatory mechanisms or validate a specific inflammatory biomarker. Independent validation and patient-level inflammatory measurements are required.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Recurrent autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) stenosis occurs in a vascular environment in which injury, neointimal hyperplasia and inflammation may coexist. Whether routine inflammatory or hematological markers contribute to clinical prognosis after drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty remains uncertain. This retrospective study examines clinical outcomes and inflammation-related prognostic associations without assuming that inflammatory pathways were measured or causally established.

title: Sex-Based Outcomes after Carotid Artery Revascularization in Symptomatic Patients: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex-based differences in outcomes after carotid revascularization remain poorly defined in symptomatic patients. We aimed to compare short and long-term outcomes between men and women with symptomatic carotid artery disease who underwent carotid revascularization across a 10-year period in 3 stroke centers.

METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on a consecutive series of cases between 2016 and 2026. Cases included patients presenting with stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), or amaurosis fugax attributable to ipsilateral carotid artery stenosis within 6 months prior carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), or transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS). Patients with prior neck radiation were excluded. Primary outcomes were stroke, TIA, myocardial infarction (MI), and death within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included long-term stroke, TIA, MI, death, restenosis, and reintervention. Both primary and secondary outcomes were analyzed individually and as a composite end point. To account for sex-based differences and vulnerable plaque feature burden, a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) analysis was performed among patients with available magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging.

RESULTS: A total of 822 procedures were performed (men: 571, 69.5%; women: 251, 30.5%) with a mean age of 73.2 ± 9.2 years. Procedure distribution was similar between groups (CEA: 69.4% vs. 70.9%; TCAR: 6.1% vs. 5.6%; TFCAS: 24.5% vs. 23.5%, P = 0.89). Demographics and comorbidities were otherwise comparable between groups. Women had higher total cholesterol (185.9 ± 50.1 vs. 158.1 ± 43.4 mg/dL, P < 0.01), high density lipoprotein (56.8 ± 18.1 vs. 45.9 ± 15.2 mg/dL, P < 0.01), and low density lipoprotein (101.5 ± 45.4 vs. 86.3 ± 38.0 mg/dL, P < 0.01); however, the low density lipoprotein/high density lipoprotein ratio was not significant. Medication regimens were similar between groups, except estrogen use, which was exclusive to women (4.0%, P < 0.01). Symptom presentation was comparable for stroke (49.0% vs. 48.6%, P = 0.91), TIA (32.0% vs. 33.5%, P = 0.69), and amaurosis fugax (22.1% vs. 20.7%, P = 0.67). At 30 days, the composite of stroke, TIA, MI, and death was similar (4.2% vs. 4.0%, P = 0.88), with no statistically significant differences in ipsilateral stroke (2.5% vs. 1.6%, P = 0.61), TIA (0.7% vs. 1.6%, P = 0.23), MI (0.5% vs. 0.0%, P = 0.25), or mortality (0.5% vs. 1.2%, P = 0.30). On long-term follow-up at 3.3 ± 2.6 years, the composite outcomes remained comparable (24.2% vs. 24.3%, P = 0.97), as were ipsilateral stroke (3.7% vs. 5.2%, P = 0.32), TIA (5.1% vs. 4.0%, P = 0.50), MI (2.6% vs. 3.6%, P = 0.45), mortality (17.5% vs. 19.1%, P = 0.58), restenosis (4.9% vs. 7.2%, P = 0.19), and reintervention rates (2.5% vs. 4.8%, P = 0.08). In the PSM cohort (men: 91, women: 91, N = 182), the 30-day (3.3% vs. 2.2%, P = 1.00) and long-term (34.1% vs. 31.9%, P = 0.88) composite outcome of stroke, TIA, MI, and death were similar. Restenosis (4.4% vs. 7.7%, P = 0.54), and reintervention (1.1% vs. 6.6%, P = 0.12) were also not statistically significantly different between groups.

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant sex-based differences were identified in 30-day or long-term outcomes after CEA, TCAR, or TFCAS across a 10-year period at 3 high-volume stroke centers. Furthermore, on propensity score matching of our highest risk patient population with vulnerable plaque features did not affect their short- and long-term outcomes.

We aimed to compare short and long-term outcomes between men and women with symptomatic carotid artery disease who underwent carotid revascularization across a 10-year period in 3 stroke centers. METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on a consecutive series of cases between 2016 and 2026.

title: Outcomes of Single-Branched TEVAR with Cervical Debranching for Zone 0 and Zone 1 Aortic Arch Repair: A VQI Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Single-branched thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) combined with cervical debranching has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open aortic arch reconstruction for patients requiring zone 0 or zone 1 proximal seal. Contemporary multicenter outcomes of this hybrid approach remain poorly defined. We evaluated procedural characteristics and perioperative outcomes of zone 0 and zone 1 single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI).

METHODS: The VQI TEVAR registry was queried to identify patients undergoing single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching. Patients were included if the proximal landing zone was 0 or 1 and distal disease was confined to zone 5 or more proximal. Chimney, fenestration, stented fenestration, custom-manufactured, and physician-modified repairs were excluded. The zone 0 cohort included patients undergoing innominate side-arm branch repair with left common carotid artery (LCCA) and left subclavian artery (LSA) bypass/transposition, whereas the zone 1 cohort included patients undergoing LCCA side-arm branch repair with LSA bypass/transposition. Outcomes were analyzed descriptively.

RESULTS: Among 38,215 TEVAR procedures screened, 50 patients met study criteria, including 39 zone 0 and 11 zone 1 repairs. The mean age was 73.8 ± 8.5 years for zone 0 and 71.7 ± 12.3 years for zone 1 patients. Prior aortic surgery was common (61.5% vs. 45.5%). Aneurysm was the most frequent indication for repair (66.7% vs. 72.7%). Staged treatment was performed in 74.4% of zone 0 and 45.5% of zone 1 procedures. The median procedure time was 166 and 163 minutes, respectively. Technical success was achieved in all patients. with no conversions to open repair and no completion type Ia or Ib endoleaks. Cerebrovascular events occurred in 2.6% of zone 0 and 18.2% of zone 1 patients, including stroke in 2.6% and 9.1%, respectively. Spinal cord ischemia occurred in one zone 0 patient (2.6%). Myocardial infarction and postoperative dialysis occurred in 10.3% and 5.1% of zone 0 patients, respectively, and in no zone 1 patients. Thirty-day mortality was 10.3% following zone 0 repair and 0% following zone 1 repair.

CONCLUSION: Single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching was feasible in selected VQI patients undergoing zone 0 and zone 1 arch repair. Given the small sample size and limited event counts, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive early outcomes rather than evidence of comparative safety or superiority. Cerebrovascular complications remain an important concern after arch endovascular intervention.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Single-branched thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) combined with cervical debranching has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open aortic arch reconstruction for patients requiring zone 0 or zone 1 proximal seal. Contemporary multicenter outcomes of this hybrid approach remain poorly defined. We evaluated procedural characteristics and perioperative outcomes of zone 0 and zone 1 single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI).

title: Revascularization of Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis: Cognitive Results of the CREST-2 Randomized Trials.
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Studies show that asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis is associated with diminished cognition. Whether carotid revascularization leads to cognitive improvement is unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether carotid revascularization improves cognition.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prespecified cognitive secondary outcomes of the CREST-2 randomized clinical trials of patients 35 years or older with 70% or greater asymptomatic carotid stenosis. Enrollment was December 2014 through July 2024, and follow-up ended July 2025. Five cognitive tests were administered before treatment and annually up to 4 years. Cognitive performances from 146 clinical sites were centrally assessed by telephone, blinded to treatment.

INTERVENTIONS: Two trials compared carotid stenting plus intensive medical management (CAS + IMM) with IMM alone and carotid endarterectomy plus IMM (CEA + IMM) with IMM alone.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Five cognitive tests, assessing learning, memory, executive function, attention, and processing speed, administered to all patients, were assessed for unadjusted and adjusted mean z scores using a linear mixed model. The minimal clinically important difference was 0.50 SD between treatment groups. The prespecified primary analysis was the fully adjusted composite z score at 4 years. Secondary analyses assessed the individual tests and at the test intervals.

RESULTS: Among 2366 US study patients, 2165 (91.5%) participated in cognitive assessments, 1078 in the CAS trial (529 CAS + IMM; 549 IMM alone) and 1087 in the CEA trial (543 CEA + IMM; 544 IMM alone); mean age was 70.1 years (SD, 7.7) and 37.8% were female. Following baseline, 4954 test batteries were administered for a mean of 2.24 (SD, 1.09) follow-up years. There were no treatment-related differences in the fully adjusted estimated composite z scores at 4 years for either the CAS trial (CAS + IMM, 0.22 [95% CI, 0.13 to 0.30] vs IMM alone, 0.18 [95% CI, 0.09 to 0.27]; between-group difference, 0.03 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.15]) or the CEA trial (CEA + IMM, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.17 to 0.33] vs IMM, 0.23 [95% CI, 0.15 to 0.32]; between-group difference, 0.02 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.14]). There were no significant differences between revascularization plus medical management vs IMM alone for any individual cognitive test.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In patients with severe asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis, revascularization with either CAS or CEA plus IMM, compared with IMM alone, did not significantly improve cognitive function at up to 4 years of follow-up.
